questions.questionText: If the perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 36 units, then its area is (in square units):
questions.solution:
Side of the equilateral triangle $a = \frac{36}{3} = 12$ units.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 12^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 144 = 36\sqrt{3} \text{ sq units}.$$

questions.questionText:
What is the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of an equilateral triangle whose perimeter is 24 cm ?
Note: Round of to the nearest two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Side $a = \frac{24}{3} = 8\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 64 = 16\sqrt{3} \approx 16 \times 1.73205 = 27.7128 \approx 27.71\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a triangle is 36 units. Its area cannot be more than ------ square units.
questions.solution:
For a given perimeter, the area of a triangle is maximized when it is equilateral.
Side $a = \frac{36}{3} = 12$ units.
$$\text{Maximum Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 12^2 = 36\sqrt{3} \text{ square units}.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of equilateral triangle is $3 \times \left(\sqrt[4]{\frac{16}{3}}\right)$ units. Determine the area of the triangle.
questions.solution:
Perimeter $P = 3a = 3 \times \left(\sqrt[4]{\frac{16}{3}}\right) \implies a = \frac{2}{3^{1/4}}$ units.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{3^{1/2}}{4} \times \frac{4}{3^{2/4}} = \frac{3^{1/2}}{4} \times \frac{4}{3^{1/2}} = 1\text{ unit}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The length of each side of an equilateral triangle is 22 cm. Find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of this triangle.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 22^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 484 = 121\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of an equilateral triangle whose sides are 12 cm.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 12^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 144 = 36\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The altitude of an equilateral triangle is $3\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. Find its area.
questions.solution:
Altitude $h = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a = 3\sqrt{3} \implies a = 6\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 36 = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ sq cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The length of the median of an equilateral triangle is $6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. What is the area of this triangle?
questions.solution:
In an equilateral triangle, median = altitude $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a = 6\sqrt{3} \implies a = 12\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 144 = 36\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Median of an equilateral triangle is $15\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. What is the length of side of this triangle?
questions.solution: Median $h = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a = 15\sqrt{3} \implies a = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: If each side of an equilateral triangle is $37\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, then its altitude (in cm) is equal to
questions.solution: $$\text{Altitude } h = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 37\sqrt{3} = \frac{37 \times 3}{2} = \frac{111}{2} = 55.5\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The height of an equilateral triangle is $7\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. What is the area of this equilateral triangle?
questions.solution:
Height $h = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a = 7\sqrt{3} \implies a = 14\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 196 = 49\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of an equilateral triangle is $289\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$. Find the length (in cm) of its sides.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = 289\sqrt{3} \implies a^2 = 289 \times 4 \implies a = 17 \times 2 = 34\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of an equilateral triangle is $4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$. Find the side (in cm) of the triangle.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = 4\sqrt{3} \implies a^2 = 16 \implies a = 4\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The length of each side of a triangle is 12 cm. What is the length of the circumradius of the triangle?
questions.solution: For an equilateral triangle, circumradius $R = \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{12}{\sqrt{3}} = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: ABC is an equilateral triangle. P, Q and R are the mid-points of sides AB, BC and CA, respectively. If the length of the side of the $\Delta\text{ABC}$ is 11 cm, then the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of $\Delta\text{PQR}$ is:
questions.solution:
The triangle formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle has area equal to $\frac{1}{4}$ of the original triangle's area.
$$\text{Area}(\Delta\text{ABC}) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 11^2 = \frac{121\sqrt{3}}{4}\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Area}(\Delta\text{PQR}) = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{121\sqrt{3}}{4} = \frac{121\sqrt{3}}{16}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a field in the shape of a Regular hexagon is $1944\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^2$. What will be the cost (in ₹) of fencing it at the rate of ₹11.50 per meter?
questions.solution:
A regular hexagon consists of 6 equilateral triangles of side $a$.
$$\text{Area} = 6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} a^2 = 1944\sqrt{3} \implies a^2 = \frac{1944 \times 2}{3} = 1296 \implies a = 36\text{ m}.$$
Perimeter $= 6 \times 36 = 216\text{ m}$.
$$\text{Cost} = 216 \times 11.50 = ₹2,484.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of triangle whose sides are 10 cm, 12 cm, and 18 cm.
questions.solution:
Semi-perimeter $s = \frac{10 + 12 + 18}{2} = 20\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{20 \times 10 \times 8 \times 2} = \sqrt{3200} = 40\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of the triangle whose sides are 3 cm, 5 cm, and 6 cm is:
questions.solution:
Semi-perimeter $s = \frac{3 + 5 + 6}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{7 \times 4 \times 2 \times 1} = \sqrt{56} = 2\sqrt{14}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: What is the area of triangular flower bed of a garden whose perimeter is 20 meters and two sides are 5 meters and 6 meters.
questions.solution:
Third side $c = 20 - 5 - 6 = 9\text{ m}$.
Semi-perimeter $s = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ m}$.
$$\text{Area} = \sqrt{10 \times (10-5) \times (10-6) \times (10-9)} = \sqrt{10 \times 5 \times 4 \times 1} = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ sq meters}.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of a triangle whose two sides are 4 cm and 5 cm and the angle between them is $45^\circ$.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a b \sin \theta = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 5 \times \sin 45^\circ = 10 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The difference between the semi-perimeter and the sides of $\Delta\text{PQR}$ are 18 cm, 17 cm and 25 cm, respectively. Find the area of the triangle.
questions.solution:
Let $s - a = 18$, $s - b = 17$, $s - c = 25$.
Summing these: $3s - (a+b+c) = 3s - 2s = s = 18 + 17 + 25 = 60\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{60 \times 18 \times 17 \times 25} = 5 \times 6 \times \sqrt{10 \times 3 \times 17} = 30\sqrt{510}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 100 cm. If the base is 36 cm, then find its semi perimeter (in centimeters).
questions.solution: $$\text{Semi-perimeter } s = \frac{\text{Perimeter}}{2} = \frac{100}{2} = 50\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 91 cm. If one of the equal sides measures 28 cm, then what is the value of the other non-equal side?
questions.solution:
Let the non-equal side be $b$. The two equal sides are each $a = 28\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2a + b = 91 \implies 2(28) + b = 91 \implies 56 + b = 91 \implies b = 35\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: In an isosceles triangle, if the unequal side is 8 cm and equal side is 5 cm. then the area of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
Height perpendicular to the unequal side (base $= 8\text{ cm}$):
$$h = \sqrt{5^2 - 4^2} = \sqrt{25 - 16} = 3\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 3 = 12\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Three sides of a triangle are $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, $\sqrt{(2a)^2+b^2}$ and $\sqrt{a^2+(2b)^2}$ units. What is the area (in unit squares) of triangle?
questions.solution:
Placing vertices on a Cartesian grid: $(0,0)$, $(2a, b)$, and $(a, 2b)$:
Side lengths are $\sqrt{(2a-0)^2 + (b-0)^2} = \sqrt{4a^2+b^2}$, $\sqrt{(a-0)^2 + (2b-0)^2} = \sqrt{a^2+4b^2}$, and $\sqrt{(2a-a)^2 + (b-2b)^2} = \sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}|x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)| = \frac{1}{2}|2a(2b) - a(b)| = \frac{1}{2}(4ab - ab) = \frac{3}{2}ab.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of the length of each equal side and the third side of an isosceles triangle is $3:5$. If the area of the triangle is $30\sqrt{11}\text{ cm}^2$ then the length of the third side (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Let the sides be $3x, 3x, 5x$. Base is $5x$.
Height $h = \sqrt{(3x)^2 - (2.5x)^2} = \sqrt{9x^2 - 6.25x^2} = \sqrt{2.75x^2} = \frac{\sqrt{11}}{2} x$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5x \times \frac{\sqrt{11}}{2} x = \frac{5\sqrt{11}}{4} x^2 = 30\sqrt{11} \implies x^2 = \frac{30 \times 4}{5} = 24 \implies x = 2\sqrt{6}.$$
Length of the third side $= 5x = 5(2\sqrt{6}) = 10\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: If the perimeter of an isosceles right triangle is $8(\sqrt{2}+1)\text{ cm}$, then the length of the hypotenuse of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
Let the equal legs be $a$, hypotenuse $h = a\sqrt{2}$.
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2a + a\sqrt{2} = a\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2} + 1) = h(\sqrt{2} + 1).$$
Given perimeter $= 8(\sqrt{2}+1)\text{ cm}$, so $h = 8\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a triangle ABC, $AB = BC$ and the perimeter of $\Delta\text{ABC}$ is $8(2+\sqrt{2})\text{ cm}$. If the length of BC is $\sqrt{2}$ times the length of AB, then find the area of $\Delta\text{ABC}$.
questions.solution:
In the triangle, $AB = AC$ and $BC = \sqrt{2} AB$. Thus $\Delta\text{ABC}$ is a right-angled isosceles triangle with right angle at A.
Perimeter $= 2(AB) + \sqrt{2}(AB) = AB(2 + \sqrt{2}) = 8(2 + \sqrt{2}) \implies AB = 8\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times AC = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 8 = 32\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A right-angled isosceles triangle has an area of 50 square units. Its hypotenuse is (in units):
questions.solution:
Let each equal leg be $a$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a^2 = 50 \implies a^2 = 100 \implies a = 10.$$
$$\text{Hypotenuse} = a\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ units}.$$

questions.questionText: In an isosceles right triangle, the perimeter is 30 m. Find its area (in $\text{m}^2$). (Rounded off to the nearest integral value)
questions.solution:
Let the equal legs be $a$. Perimeter $= a(2 + \sqrt{2}) = 30$.
$$a = \frac{30}{2 + \sqrt{2}} = \frac{30(2 - \sqrt{2})}{2} = 15(2 - \sqrt{2}) \approx 15(2 - 1.4142) = 15(0.5858) \approx 8.787\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 225 \times (6 - 4\sqrt{2}) = 225(3 - 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 225(3 - 2.8284) = 225(0.1716) \approx 38.61 \approx 39\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of an isosceles right-angled triangle having an area of $200\text{ cm}^2$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a^2 = 200 \implies a^2 = 400 \implies a = 20\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Hypotenuse} = a\sqrt{2} = 20\sqrt{2} \approx 20 \times 1.4142 = 28.28\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2a + a\sqrt{2} = 40 + 28.28 = 68.28 \approx 68.3\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of an isosceles right angled triangle is $16\text{ m}^2$. Its hypotenuse is
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a^2 = 16 \implies a^2 = 32.$$
$$\text{Hypotenuse} = \sqrt{2a^2} = \sqrt{2 \times 32} = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of a triangle whose base is 7 cm and corresponding height is 82 cm.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 82 = 7 \times 41 = 287\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: If the area of a triangle whose base measures 6 cm is $18\text{ cm}^2$, then its height is:
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times b \times h = 18 \implies \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times h = 18 \implies 3h = 18 \implies h = 6\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: If three sides of a triangle are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, then the area of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
Since $6^2 + 8^2 = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10^2$, this is a right-angled triangle.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 12 cm, 13 cm and 5 cm?
questions.solution:
Since $5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13^2$, it is a right-angled triangle.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The sides of a triangle are of length 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm. Find the area of the triangle.
questions.solution:
Since $8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17^2$, it is a right-angled triangle.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 15 = 60\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio $5:12:13$ and its perimeter is 90 cm. Find its area (in $\text{cm}^2$).
questions.solution:
Sum of ratio terms $= 5 + 12 + 13 = 30$ units $= 90\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ unit} = 3\text{ cm}$.
Sides are $15\text{ cm}, 36\text{ cm}, 39\text{ cm}$.
Since $15^2 + 36^2 = 39^2$, it is a right-angled triangle.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 36 = 270\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The lengths of three sides of a triangle are in the ratio $3:4:5$. Among three sides, the difference between the largest side and the smallest side of this triangle is 3.6cm. The area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
Let sides be $3x, 4x, 5x$. Largest $-$ smallest $= 5x - 3x = 2x = 3.6\text{ cm} \implies x = 1.8\text{ cm}$.
Sides are $3(1.8) = 5.4\text{ cm}$, $4(1.8) = 7.2\text{ cm}$, $5(1.8) = 9.0\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5.4 \times 7.2 = 19.44\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A right angle triangle of area $600\text{ m}^2$ is to be made such that the hypotenuse is double the base. For the triangle, the hypotenuse is ------ more than the base.
questions.solution:
Let base $= b$, hypotenuse $= 2b$. Perpendicular $= \sqrt{(2b)^2 - b^2} = b\sqrt{3}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times b \times b\sqrt{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} b^2 = 600 \implies b^2 = \frac{1200}{\sqrt{3}} = 400\sqrt{3} \approx 692.82 \implies b \approx 26.32\text{ m}.$$
Hypotenuse $-$ base $= 2b - b = b \approx 26.32\text{ m}$.

questions.questionText: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is 6m more than twice the shortest side. If the third side is 2 m less than the hypotenuse, find the area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the triangle
questions.solution:
Let shortest side be $x$. Hypotenuse $= 2x + 6$, third side $= 2x + 4$.
By Pythagoras theorem:
$$x^2 + (2x + 4)^2 = (2x + 6)^2$$
$$x^2 + 4x^2 + 16x + 16 = 4x^2 + 24x + 36 \implies x^2 - 8x - 20 = 0 \implies (x - 10)(x + 2) = 0 \implies x = 10\text{ m}.$$
Sides are 10 m and $2(10) + 4 = 24\text{ m}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 24 = 120\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Find the height of the triangle whose base is two-thirds of its height and whose area is $363\text{ cm}^2$.
questions.solution:
Base $b = \frac{2}{3} h$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times b \times h = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} h \times h = \frac{1}{3} h^2 = 363 \implies h^2 = 1089 \implies h = 33\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: A triangle has its sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm. What will be the area of the triangle formed by joining the mid point of the three sides?
questions.solution:
Original triangle is right-angled with sides 5, 12, 13.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30\text{ cm}^2.$$
The triangle formed by joining midpoints has area $\frac{1}{4}$ of original:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{30}{4} = 7.5 = 7\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: In $\Delta\text{ABC}$, $\text{BD} \perp \text{AC}$, intersecting AC at D. Also, $\text{BD} = 12\text{ cm}$. If $\text{m(AD)} = 6\text{ cm}$ and $\text{m(CD)} = 4\text{ cm}$, find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of $\Delta\text{ABC}$.
questions.solution:
Base $AC = AD + CD = 6 + 4 = 10\text{ cm}$. Height $BD = 12\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BD = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 12 = 60\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: In a right-angled triangle, if the hypotenuse is 101 cm and one of its sides is equal to 20 cm, what is its area (in $\text{cm}^2$)?
questions.solution:
The other perpendicular side is:
$$\sqrt{101^2 - 20^2} = \sqrt{(101 - 20)(101 + 20)} = \sqrt{81 \times 121} = 9 \times 11 = 99\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 99 = 990\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The sides of a triangle are 24 cm, 26 cm and 10 cm, At each of its vertices, circles of radius 4.2 cm are drawn. What is the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the triangle, excluding the portion covered by the sectors of the circles? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
Since $10^2 + 24^2 = 26^2$, it is a right-angled triangle.
$$\text{Area of triangle} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 24 = 120\text{ cm}^2.$$
The sum of the sector angles at the vertices of any triangle is $180^\circ$ (semi-circle):
$$\text{Area of sectors} = \frac{1}{2} \pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 4.2 \times 4.2 = 11 \times 0.6 \times 4.2 = 27.72\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Remaining area} = 120 - 27.72 = 92.28\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: $\Delta\text{ABC}$ is a right-angled triangle with $\angle\text{ABC} = 90^\circ$. If $\text{m}(\overline{\text{AB}}) = 28\text{ cm}$, and $\text{m}(\overline{\text{BC}}) = 96\text{ cm}$, find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the circumcircle of $\Delta\text{ABC}$. (Use $\pi = 3.14$).
questions.solution:
Hypotenuse $AC = \sqrt{28^2 + 96^2} = \sqrt{784 + 9216} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\text{ cm}$.
Circumradius of right triangle $R = \frac{\text{Hypotenuse}}{2} = 50\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \pi R^2 = 3.14 \times 50^2 = 3.14 \times 2500 = 7850\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText:
What is the difference in area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of $\Delta\text{ABC}$ having sides of 10 cm, 20 cm and 20 cm, and a right angled $\Delta\text{PQR}$ with hypotenuse of 13 cm and one of the perpendiculars of 12 cm?
Note: $\sqrt{2} = 1.41$, $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$, $\sqrt{7} = 2.65$, $\sqrt{13} = 3.61$, $\sqrt{15} = 3.87$, $\sqrt{21} = 4.58$
questions.solution:
For $\Delta\text{ABC}$ (isosceles with sides 20, 20, 10):
Altitude to base 10 is $h = \sqrt{20^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{375} = 5\sqrt{15} \approx 5 \times 3.87 = 19.35\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area}(\Delta\text{ABC}) = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 19.35 = 96.75\text{ cm}^2.$$
For right-angled $\Delta\text{PQR}$ (hypotenuse 13, perpendicular 12):
Other perpendicular $= \sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = 5\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area}(\Delta\text{PQR}) = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 5 = 30\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Difference} = 96.75 - 30 = 66.75\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The in-radius of triangle is 8 cm, and the sum of the lengths of its sides is 125 cm. The area of the triangle (in $\text{cm}^2$) is:
questions.solution:
Semi-perimeter $s = \frac{125}{2} = 62.5\text{ cm}$. In-radius $r = 8\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = r \times s = 8 \times 62.5 = 500\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Find the circumference of a circle whose area is $154\text{ m}^2$.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} r^2 = 154 \implies r^2 = 49 \implies r = 7\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Circumference} = 2\pi r = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 44\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The circumference of the two circles is 198 cm and 352 cm respectively. What is the difference between their radii?
questions.solution: $$2\pi R - 2\pi r = 352 - 198 = 154 \implies 2 \times \frac{22}{7} (R - r) = 154 \implies R - r = \frac{154 \times 7}{44} = 24.5\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a circle is $1386\text{ cm}^2$. What is the radius of the circle? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} r^2 = 1386 \implies r^2 = \frac{1386 \times 7}{22} = 63 \times 7 = 441 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The radii of two circles are 8 cm and 15 cm. The perimeter of the circle having area equal to the sum of the areas of the two circles (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
$$\pi R^2 = \pi (8^2) + \pi (15^2) = \pi (64 + 225) = 289\pi \implies R = 17\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2\pi R = 2\pi (17) = 34\pi\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Find the diameter (in cm) of a circle whose circumference is equal to the sum of the circumferences of two circles of radii 12 cm and 16 cm.
questions.solution:
$$2\pi R = 2\pi(12) + 2\pi(16) = 2\pi(28) \implies R = 28\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Diameter} = 2R = 56\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of circumference and diameter of a circle is $3:5$. If the circumference is 6 cm, then the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Given $\frac{\text{Circumference}}{\text{Diameter}} = \frac{3}{5}$.
If Circumference $= 6\text{ cm}$, then Diameter $= 6 \times \frac{5}{3} = 10\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Radius} = \frac{\text{Diameter}}{2} = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines touch the circles at P and Q. Area of the circle is $154\text{cm}^2$. Find the length of PQ. [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
The distance between two parallel tangents PQ is the diameter of the circle.
$$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} r^2 = 154 \implies r^2 = 49 \implies r = 7\text{ cm}.$$
$$PQ = 2r = 14\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The circumference of the two circles is 264 m and 308 m respectively. What is the difference between the area of the larger circle and the smaller circle?
questions.solution:
$$2\pi R = 308 \implies R = \frac{308 \times 7}{44} = 49\text{ m}, \quad 2\pi r = 264 \implies r = \frac{264 \times 7}{44} = 42\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Difference in area} = \pi (R^2 - r^2) = \frac{22}{7} (49 - 42)(49 + 42) = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 91 = 22 \times 91 = 2002\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A race track is in the shape of a ring whose inner and outer circumferences are 880 m and 1012 m, respectively. What is the area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the track? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$2\pi R = 1012 \implies R = \frac{1012 \times 7}{44} = 161\text{ m}, \quad 2\pi r = 880 \implies r = \frac{880 \times 7}{44} = 140\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \pi(R^2 - r^2) = \frac{22}{7} (161 - 140)(161 + 140) = \frac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 301 = 66 \times 301 = 19866\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of areas of two circles is $81:121$. What will be the ratio of their circumferences?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{\text{Area}_1}{\text{Area}_2} = \frac{r_1^2}{r_2^2} = \frac{81}{121} \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{9}{11}.$$
$$\frac{\text{Circumference}_1}{\text{Circumference}_2} = \frac{2\pi r_1}{2\pi r_2} = \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{9}{11}.$$

questions.questionText: The cost of building a fence around a circular field is ₹7425 at the rate of ₹13.50 per feet. What is the area of the circular field? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$\text{Circumference} = \frac{7425}{13.5} = 550\text{ ft}.$$
$$2 \times \frac{22}{7} r = 550 \implies r = \frac{550 \times 7}{44} = 87.5\text{ ft}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times (87.5)^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 7656.25 = 24062.5\text{ ft}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The difference between the areas of two concentric circles is $88\text{ cm}^2$. If the radius of the inner circle is 6 cm, then the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the larger circle is closest to: [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area of inner circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 6^2 = \frac{792}{7} \approx 113.14\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Area of larger circle} = 113.14 + 88 = 201.14 \approx 201\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of circular park is $12474\text{ m}^2$. There is 3.5 m wide path around the park. What is the area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the path? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area of park} = \frac{22}{7} r^2 = 12474 \implies r^2 = \frac{12474 \times 7}{22} = 3969 \implies r = 63\text{ m}.$$
Outer radius $R = 63 + 3.5 = 66.5\text{ m}$.
$$\text{Area of path} = \pi (R^2 - r^2) = \frac{22}{7} (66.5 - 63)(66.5 + 63) = \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 129.5 = 11 \times 129.5 = 1424.5\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a circular path enclosed by two concentric circles is $3080\text{ m}^2$. If the difference between the radius of the outer edge and that of inner edge of the circular path is 10 m, what is the sum (in m) of the two radii?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \pi(R^2 - r^2) = \frac{22}{7} (R - r)(R + r) = 3080.$$
Given $R - r = 10\text{ m}$:
$$\frac{22}{7} \times 10 \times (R + r) = 3080 \implies R + r = \frac{3080 \times 7}{220} = 98\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: A 64 cm wide path is made around a circular garden having a diameter of 10 meters. The area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the path is closest to: [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
Inner radius $r = 5\text{ m}$. Outer radius $R = 5 + 0.64 = 5.64\text{ m}$.
$$\text{Area} = \pi(R^2 - r^2) = \frac{22}{7} \times 0.64 \times 10.64 = \frac{22}{7} \times 6.8096 \approx 21.4 \approx 21\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A race track is in the shape of a ring whose inner and outer circumference is 440m and 506 m, respectively. What is the cost of levelling the track at ₹$6/\text{m}^2$? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]

The area of a circular path enclosed by two concentric circles is $3080\text{ m}^2$. If the difference between the radius of the outer edge and that of inner edge of the circular path is 10 m, what is the sum (in m) of the two radii? [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \pi(R - r)(R + r) = 3080 \implies \frac{22}{7} \times 10 \times (R + r) = 3080 \implies R + r = 98\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The sum of the radii of two circles is 286cm and the area between the concentric circles is $50336\text{ cm}^2$. What are the radii (in cm) of the two circles? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$R + r = 286\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} (R + r)(R - r) = 50336 \implies \frac{22}{7} \times 286 \times (R - r) = 50336 \implies R - r = 56\text{ cm}.$$
$$R = \frac{286 + 56}{2} = 171\text{ cm}, \quad r = \frac{286 - 56}{2} = 115\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The inner and outer radii of a circular track are 25 m and 28 m, respectively. The cost (in) of levelling the track at $\text{Rs.} 28\text{ per m}^2$ is: [Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} (28^2 - 25^2) = \frac{22}{7} \times 3 \times 53 = \frac{22 \times 159}{7}\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Cost} = 28 \times \frac{22 \times 159}{7} = 4 \times 22 \times 159 = 88 \times 159 = 13992\text{ Rs}.$$

questions.questionText: Two equal circles are drawn on a square in such a way that opposite side of the square forms the diameter of each circle. If the remaining area of the square is $42\text{ cm}^2$, what is the measurement (in cm) of the diameter of each circle?
questions.solution:
Let side of square be $a$. The two semicircles together form a full circle of diameter $a$ (radius $r = \frac{a}{2}$).
$$\text{Remaining area} = a^2 - \pi \left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2 = a^2 - \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{a^2}{4} = a^2 \left(1 - \frac{11}{14}\right) = \frac{3}{14} a^2 = 42.$$
$$a^2 = 42 \times \frac{14}{3} = 196 \implies a = 14\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Diameter} = a = 14\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: From a circular sheet of cirumference 264 cm, two equal maximum-sized circular plates are cut off. What will be the circumference of each plate? $\left[\text{Use }\pi = \frac{22}{7}\right]$
questions.solution:
Circumference $2\pi R = 264 \implies R = \frac{264 \times 7}{44} = 42\text{ cm}$.
Diameter of the sheet $= 2R = 84\text{ cm}$.
Two maximum-sized equal circular plates lie along the diameter, so diameter of each plate $d = \frac{84}{2} = 42\text{ cm}$ (radius $r = 21\text{ cm}$).
$$\text{Circumference} = 2\pi r = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 = 132\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: A chord of the larger among two concentric circles is of length 20 cm and it is tangent to the smaller circle. What is the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the circular portion between the two circles?
questions.solution:
In right triangle formed by radii $R$, $r$ and half-chord $L/2 = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$R^2 - r^2 = 10^2 = 100.$$
$$\text{Area of circular ring} = \pi (R^2 - r^2) = 100\pi\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Two circles of radius 7 units each, intersect in such a way that the common chord is of length 7 units. What is the common area in square units of the intersection?
questions.solution:
The common chord and radii form an equilateral triangle of side $r = 7$, subtending angle $60^\circ$ at both centres.
$$\text{Area of each segment} = \text{Area of sector} - \text{Area of triangle} = \pi r^2 \left(\frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ}\right) - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} r^2 = r^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right).$$
$$\text{Total common area} = 2 \times r^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) = 2 \times 49 \left(\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) = 98\left(\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right).$$

questions.questionText: The area of the largest triangle that can be inscribed in a semi-circle of radius 6 cm is:
questions.solution:
The largest triangle inscribed in a semicircle has the diameter as base ($2r$) and radius as height ($r$).
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times (2r) \times r = r^2 = 6^2 = 36\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Three circles of radius 7 cm are kept touching each other. The string is tightly tied around these three circles. What is the length of the string?
questions.solution:
Length of string tied around 3 identical mutually touching circles of radius $r$:
$$\text{Length} = 2\pi r + 6r = 2\pi(7) + 6(7) = 42 + 14\pi\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Three circles each of radius 5 cm touch one another. The area (in $\text{cm}^2$) subtended between them is:
questions.solution:
The equilateral triangle joining the centres has side $2r = 10\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area of equilateral triangle} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (2r)^2 = \sqrt{3} r^2.$$
$$\text{Area of 3 sectors of } 60^\circ = 3 \times \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} \pi r^2 = \frac{\pi r^2}{2}.$$
$$\text{Enclosed area} = r^2 \left(\sqrt{3} - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 25\left(\sqrt{3} - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of a circle with a maximum radius that can be inscribed in a rectangle of length 18 cm and breadth 12 cm.
questions.solution:
Maximum radius of a circle inscribed in a rectangle $= \frac{\text{breadth}}{2} = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 = \pi (6^2) = 36\pi\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of biggest circle that could be drawn in a square of side 18 cm is:
questions.solution:
Radius of biggest inscribed circle $r = \frac{\text{side}}{2} = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 = \pi (9^2) = 81\pi\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: One-quarter of a circular pizza of radius 21 cm was removed from the whole pizza. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the remaining pizza? $\left(\text{Use }\pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Length of $\frac{3}{4}$ arc $= \frac{3}{4} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 = \frac{3}{4} \times 132 = 99\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{arc length} + 2r = 99 + 2(21) = 99 + 42 = 141\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: A copper wire is bent in the form of a square and it encloses an area of $30.25\text{ cm}^2$. If the same wire is bent to form a circle, then find the area of the circle.
questions.solution:
Side of square $a = \sqrt{30.25} = 5.5\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Length of wire} = 4a = 4 \times 5.5 = 22\text{ cm}.$$
$$2\pi r = 22 \implies 2 \times \frac{22}{7} r = 22 \implies r = 3.5\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 12.25 = 38.50\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: When a wire is bent in the form of a square, then the area enclosed by it is $5929\text{ cm}^2$. If wire is bent into the form of a circle, then what will be the area enclosed by the wire?
questions.solution:
Side of square $a = \sqrt{5929} = 77\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Perimeter} = 4 \times 77 = 308\text{ cm}.$$
$$2 \times \frac{22}{7} r = 308 \implies r = \frac{308 \times 7}{44} = 49\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 49^2 = 22 \times 7 \times 49 = 7546\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Three circles of radius 6 cm are kept touching each other. The string is tightly tied around these three circles. What is the length of the string?
questions.solution: $$\text{Length of string} = 6r + 2\pi r = 6(6) + 2\pi(6) = 36 + 12\pi\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: A smaller circle touches a bigger circle internally and also passes through the center 'O' of the bigger circle. If the area of the smaller circle is $192\text{ cm}^2$, the area of the bigger circle (in $\text{cm}^2$) is:
questions.solution:
The diameter of the smaller circle equals the radius of the bigger circle, so $R = 2r$.
$$\text{Area of bigger circle} = \pi R^2 = \pi (2r)^2 = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times 192 = 768\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a triangular park, whose sides are 160 m, 300 m and 340 m, is $4\frac{17}{22}$ times the area of a circular park. What is the perimeter (in m) of the circular park (correct to one decimal place)? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
Since $160^2 + 300^2 = 25600 + 90000 = 115600 = 340^2$, the triangular park is right-angled.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 160 \times 300 = 24000\text{ m}^2.$$
$$4\frac{17}{22} = \frac{105}{22}.$$
$$\frac{105}{22} \times \pi r^2 = 24000 \implies \frac{105}{22} \times \frac{22}{7} r^2 = 15 r^2 = 24000 \implies r^2 = 1600 \implies r = 40\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2\pi r = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 40 = \frac{1760}{7} \approx 251.4\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The side of an equilateral triangle is 28 cm. Taking each vertex as the centre, a circle is described with a radius equal to half the length of the side of the triangle. Find the area of that part of the triangle which is not included in the circles (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$).
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area of triangle} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 28^2 = 196 \times 1.73 = 339.08\text{ cm}^2.$$
Radius of sectors $r = 14\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area of 3 sectors} = \frac{180^\circ}{360^\circ} \pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 11 \times 28 = 308\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Remaining area} = 339.08 - 308 = 31.08\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: What is the radius (in m) of a circular field whose area is equal to six times the area of a triangular field whose sides are 35 m, 53 m and 66 m ? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$s = \frac{35 + 53 + 66}{2} = 77\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area of triangle} = \sqrt{77 \times (77-35) \times (77-53) \times (77-66)} = \sqrt{77 \times 42 \times 24 \times 11}$$
$$= \sqrt{11 \times 7 \times 7 \times 6 \times 6 \times 4 \times 11} = 11 \times 7 \times 6 \times 2 = 924\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\pi r^2 = 6 \times 924 = 5544 \implies \frac{22}{7} r^2 = 5544 \implies r^2 = 252 \times 7 = 1764 \implies r = 42\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is $17:15$. If path is 40 meters wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{R}{r} = \frac{17}{15} \implies R - r = 2x = 40\text{ m} \implies x = 20\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Inner radius } r = 15x = 15 \times 20 = 300\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is $5:4$. If path is 50 metres wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{R}{r} = \frac{5}{4} \implies R - r = 1x = 50\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Inner radius } r = 4x = 4 \times 50 = 200\text{ meters}.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is $7:6$. If the path is 45 m wide, then what is the radius (in m) of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
$$\frac{R}{r} = \frac{7}{6} \implies R - r = 1x = 45\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Inner radius } r = 6x = 6 \times 45 = 270\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The diameter of a wheel is 1.33 m. What distance (in m, to the nearest whole number) will it travel in 380 revolutions? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Distance} = N \times \pi d = 380 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 1.33 = 380 \times 22 \times 0.19 = 1588.4 \approx 1588\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: A wheel makes 500 revolutions in covering a distance of 44 km. Find the radius of the wheel
questions.solution:
$$\text{Distance} = 44\text{ km} = 44000\text{ m}.$$
$$500 \times 2\pi r = 44000 \implies 1000 \times \frac{22}{7} r = 44000 \implies r = \frac{44 \times 7}{22} = 14\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: If a wheel has diameter 42 cm, then how far does the wheel go (in meters) in 12 revolutions? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Distance} = 12 \times \pi d = 12 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 0.42\text{ m} = 12 \times 22 \times 0.06 = 15.84\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: If a map of a city was drawn on a scale of 0.2 cm to a km, what area would represent a country if it has an area of $22500\text{km}^2$?
questions.solution:
$$1\text{ km} = 0.2\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ km}^2 = (0.2)^2\text{ cm}^2 = 0.04\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Map Area} = 22500 \times 0.04 = 900\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a semi-circle is 56.54 cm. What is its diameter (in cm)? (Use $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \pi r + 2r = r(\pi + 2) = r(3.14 + 2) = 5.14 r = 56.54 \implies r = \frac{56.54}{5.14} = 11\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Diameter} = 2r = 22\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Akshay places three identical rings of diameter 21 cm in such a manner that each one touches the other two rings. He observes that there is a space enclosed by the circles. What is the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of this portion? (Take $\pi = 22/7$) Note: Rounded off to nearest 2 decimal places and $\sqrt{3} = 1.732$
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 10.5\text{ cm}$. The area enclosed between three mutually touching circles is:
$$\text{Area} = \left(\sqrt{3} - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) r^2 = \left(1.732 - \frac{11}{7}\right) \times 110.25 = (1.732 - 1.5714) \times 110.25 = 0.1606 \times 110.25 \approx 17.70\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the circle?

options.label: A
options.text: The area of a sector = $\frac{1}{2}\text{ (arc length} \times \text{R)}$

options.label: B
options.text: The length of an arc = $\frac{\text{central angle made by the arc}}{360^\circ}$

options.label: C
options.text: The radius of an incircle of an equilateral triangle of side 's' is $\frac{s}{2\sqrt{3}}$

options.label: D
options.text: Circles are congruent if they have same radii while similar circles may have different radii.

questions.solution: The correct formula for the length of an arc is $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi R$. Statement (B) omits the factor $2\pi R$, making it INCORRECT.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The central angle of a sector is $80^\circ$ and length is $96\pi$. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution: $$\text{Arc length } l = 2\pi r \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = 2\pi r \times \frac{80^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{4\pi r}{9} = 96\pi \implies \frac{4r}{9} = 96 \implies r = 216\text{ units}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: From a circle, a sector with a central angle of $30^\circ$ is cut off. If the length of the arc of this sector is 5.5 cm, then find the radius (in cm) of the circle. $\left[\text{Use }\pi = \frac{22}{7}\right]$
questions.solution: $$l = 2\pi r \times \frac{30^\circ}{360^\circ} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \times \frac{1}{12} = \frac{11r}{21} = 5.5 \implies r = \frac{5.5 \times 21}{11} = 10.5\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText:
The following formula is used to calculate which of the following?
$$\frac{\text{angle of arc at centre}}{360^\circ} \times \pi \times \text{diameter}$$
questions.solution: $$\frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi d = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r = \text{Length of an arc}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: An arc of length 23.1 cm subtends an $18^\circ$ angle at the center. What is the area of the circle? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$l = 2\pi r \times \frac{18^\circ}{360^\circ} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \times \frac{1}{20} = \frac{11r}{35} = 23.1 \implies r = \frac{23.1 \times 35}{11} = 73.5\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times (73.5)^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 5402.25 = 16978.50\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the length of the arc of the sector of a circle of diameter 7 cm with a central angle of $108^\circ$. [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Arc length} = \pi d \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times \frac{108^\circ}{360^\circ} = 22 \times \frac{3}{10} = 6.6\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: In a circle of radius 42 cm, an arc subtends an angle of $60^\circ$ at the center. Find the length of the arc. [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Arc length } l = 2\pi r \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 42 \times \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} = 2 \times 22 \times 6 \times \frac{1}{6} = 44\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A coconut tree swings with the wind in such a manner that the angle covered by its trunk is $18^\circ$. If the topmost portion of the tree covers a distance of 44 meters, find the length of the tree.
questions.solution: $$\text{Distance } l = 2\pi r \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \times \frac{18^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{44r}{70} = 44 \implies r = 70 \times \frac{44}{44} = 140\text{ meters}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: If the arc of a circle of radius 30 cm has a length of 19 cm, then the angle (in degrees, rounded off to two decimal places) subtended at the center of the circle is: [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\theta = \frac{l \times 360^\circ}{2\pi r} = \frac{19 \times 360^\circ}{2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 30} = \frac{19 \times 6 \times 7}{44} = \frac{798}{22} \approx 36.27^\circ.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The area of a sector of a circle is 88 sq. cm., and the angle of the sector is $45^\circ$. Find the radius of the circle [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{7} r^2 \times \frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{56} r^2 = 88 \implies r^2 = 4 \times 56 = 224 \implies r = \sqrt{224} = 4\sqrt{14}\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The area of a sector of a circle is $88\text{ cm}^2$ and the angle of the sector is $36^\circ$. Find the radius (in cm) of the circle. [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} r^2 \times \frac{36^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{70} r^2 = 88 \implies r^2 = 4 \times 70 = 280 \implies r = \sqrt{280} = 2\sqrt{70}\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The area of a sector of a circle that subtends a $22.5^\circ$ angle at the center is given as $346.5\text{ cm}^2$. What will be the radius (in cm) of the circle? [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$\frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \frac{22.5^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{16}.$$
$$\frac{22}{7} r^2 \times \frac{1}{16} = 346.5 \implies r^2 = \frac{346.5 \times 112}{22} = 15.75 \times 112 = 1764 \implies r = 42\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The area of the sector of a circle of radius 12 cm is $32\pi\text{ cm}^2$. Find the length of the corresponding arc of the sector.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r \implies 32\pi = \frac{1}{2} \times l \times 12 = 6l \implies l = \frac{32\pi}{6} = \frac{16}{3}\pi\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the area of the sector of a circle with radius 4 cm and angle $30^\circ$.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \pi \times 16 \times \frac{30^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{4\pi}{3} \approx \frac{4 \times 3.14159}{3} \approx 4.186\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: From a circle with the radius of 15.75 cm, a sector with the arc length of 11 cm is cut off. Find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of this sector.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 11 \times 15.75 = 5.5 \times 15.75 = 86.625\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the area of a sector with an arc length of 44 cm, which subtends a central angle of $30^\circ$.
questions.solution:
$$l = 2\pi r \times \frac{30^\circ}{360^\circ} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \times \frac{1}{12} = \frac{11r}{21} = 44 \implies r = 84\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 44 \times 84 = 1848\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: For a given circle of radius 4 cm, the angle of its sector is $45^\circ$. Find the area (in cm) of the sector. (Use $\pi = 3.14$.)
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 \times \frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} = 3.14 \times 16 \times \frac{1}{8} = 3.14 \times 2 = 6.28\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the sector of a circle of radius 21 cm with a central angle of $60^\circ$. [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 \times \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{7} \times 441 \times \frac{1}{6} = 22 \times 63 \times \frac{1}{6} = 11 \times 21 = 231\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: What is the area of the sector of a circle whose radius is 35 cm and whose arc subtends an angle of $72^\circ$ at the center of the circle? [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times 35^2 \times \frac{72^\circ}{360^\circ} = 22 \times 5 \times 35 \times \frac{1}{5} = 22 \times 35 = 770\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A sector of a circle of radius 10 cm is formed at $60^\circ$ angle at the center. What will be its area (Take $\pi = 3.14$)?
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = 3.14 \times 10^2 \times \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{314}{6} \approx 52.33\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the sector whose perimeter is $\frac{64}{3}\text{ cm}$ and central angle is $60^\circ$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + 2\pi r \times \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} = 2r + \frac{22r}{21} = \frac{64r}{21} = \frac{64}{3} \implies r = 7\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{154}{6} = \frac{77}{3}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the measure of the central angle of a sector if its area is $16\pi$ and the radius is 8.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \pi r^2 \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \pi \times 64 \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = 16\pi \implies \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \frac{16}{64} = \frac{1}{4} \implies \theta = 90^\circ.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: If the area of a sector of a circle is $462\text{ cm}^2$ and the central angle is $120^\circ$, then its radius is ------.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} r^2 \times \frac{120^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{21} r^2 = 462 \implies r^2 = \frac{462 \times 21}{22} = 21 \times 21 = 441 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The area of sector of a circle having radius 14 cm is $231\text{ cm}^2$. Find the degree measure of the corresponding central angle. [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = 616 \times \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = 231 \implies \theta = \frac{231 \times 360^\circ}{616} = \frac{3 \times 360^\circ}{8} = 135^\circ.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: What is the perimeter (in cm, rounded off to one decimal place) of the sector of a circle with a radius of 10 cm and of angle $30^\circ$? (Use $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
$$l = 2\pi r \times \frac{30^\circ}{360^\circ} = 2 \times 3.14 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{12} = \frac{62.8}{12} \approx 5.23\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 20 + 5.23 = 25.23 \approx 25.2\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A circular arc whose radius is 12 cm makes an angle of $30^\circ$ at the centre. Find the perimeter (in cm) of the sector formed. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
$$l = 2 \times 3.14 \times 12 \times \frac{30^\circ}{360^\circ} = 6.28\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 24 + 6.28 = 30.28\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A circular arc makes an angle of $15^\circ$ at the centre, If the radius of the circular arc is 14 cm, what is the perimeter (correct up to two decimal places) of the sector so formed? ($\pi = 3.14$)?
questions.solution:
$$l = 2 \times 3.14 \times 14 \times \frac{15^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{87.92}{24} \approx 3.66\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 28 + 3.66 = 31.66\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A circular arc whose radius is 24 cm makes and angle of $60^\circ$ at the centre. The perimeter of the sector formed is: (Use $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
$$l = 2 \times 3.14 \times 24 \times \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} = 25.12\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 48 + 25.12 = 73.12\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A circular arc whose radius is 14 cm, makes an angle of $45^\circ$ at the centre. Find the perimeter (in cm) of the sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution:
$$l = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 \times \frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} = 88 \times \frac{1}{8} = 11\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 28 + 11 = 39\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The perimeter of a minor sector of a circle of radius 4 units subtending an angle of $45^\circ$ is:
questions.solution:
$$l = 2\pi(4) \times \frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} = 8\pi \times \frac{1}{8} = \pi\text{ units}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 8 + \pi\text{ units}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: If the angle of the sector with radius 7 cm is $120^\circ$ then find the length of the sector (in cm). (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution: $$\text{Length of arc } l = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times \frac{120^\circ}{360^\circ} = 44 \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{44}{3}\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: A circular arc whose radius is 4 cm makes an angle $45^\circ$ at the center. Find the perimeter of the sector formed.
questions.solution:
$$l = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 4 \times \frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{22}{7}\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 2(4) + \frac{22}{7} = 8 + \frac{22}{7} = \frac{78}{7}\text{ cm}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the perimeter of major sector of a circle of radius 12 meters, whose minor sector subtends an angle of $75^\circ$ at the center.
questions.solution:
Angle of major sector $= 360^\circ - 75^\circ = 285^\circ$.
$$\text{Arc length} = 2\pi(12) \times \frac{285^\circ}{360^\circ} = 24\pi \times \frac{19}{24} = 19\pi\text{ meters}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + \text{arc length} = 24 + 19\pi\text{ meters}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 12 cm, formed by an arc of length 7 cm is:
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 12 = 42\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the sector, where the radius of the circle is 24 cm and length of the arc is 7 cm.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 24 = 84\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: What is the area (in square units) of the sector if the radius of the circle is given to be 24 units and the arc length is 7.5 units?
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 7.5 \times 24 = 90\text{ square units}.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: If the radius of a circle is 48 cm and the length of the arc is 15 cm, then the area of the sector corresponding to that arc is:
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 48 = 360\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: Find the area of a minor sector of a circle whose circumference is 88 cm and the length of its minor arc is 22 cm [Use $\pi = 22/7$].
questions.solution:
$$2\pi r = 88 \implies r = \frac{88 \times 7}{44} = 14\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 22 \times 14 = 154\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius 7.4 cm is 20.6 cm. The area of this sector is:

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The perimeter of a minor sector of a circle of radius 5 cm is 15.5 cm. Find the area of the minor sector [Use $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$l = \text{Perimeter} - 2r = 15.5 - 2(5) = 5.5\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} \times 5.5 \times 5 = 13.75\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: What is the central angle of a sector of a circle whose area and perimeter are, respectively, equal to $209\text{ cm}^2$ and 63 cm if it is given that its radius is a non-negative integer (roundup to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2r + l = 63 \implies l = 63 - 2r.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} l r = \frac{1}{2} r (63 - 2r) = 209 \implies 2r^2 - 63r + 418 = 0.$$
Solving the quadratic for integer $r$:
$$r = \frac{63 \pm \sqrt{63^2 - 4(2)(418)}}{4} = \frac{63 \pm \sqrt{3969 - 3344}}{4} = \frac{63 \pm 25}{4} \implies r = 22\text{ cm}.$$
Then $l = 63 - 44 = 19\text{ cm}$.
$$\theta = \frac{l \times 360^\circ}{2\pi r} = \frac{19 \times 360^\circ \times 7}{2 \times 22 \times 22} = \frac{47880}{968} \approx 49.46^\circ \approx 49.5^\circ.$$

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
questions.questionText: The minute hand of a clock is 20 cm long. Find the area on the surface of the clock swept by the minute hand between 8 a.m. and 8:45 a.m.
questions.solution:
Angle swept in 45 minutes $= 45 \times 6^\circ = 270^\circ = \frac{3}{4} \times 360^\circ$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{3}{4} \pi r^2 = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 20^2 = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 400 = 300 \times \frac{22}{7} = \frac{6600}{7}\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Let ABCD be a quadrilateral and AC, BD be diagonals. The length of $\text{BD} = 20\text{ cm}$ and the heights of the $\Delta\text{ABD}$ and $\Delta\text{BCD}$ are 6 cm and 8 cm respectively. Find the area of the quadrilateral ABCD (in $\text{cm}^2$).
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{BD} \times (h_1 + h_2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times (6 + 8) = 10 \times 14 = 140\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: There is a circle with a centre T and a radius of 8 cm. Two tangents KE and KI are drawn from point K, which is 17 cm from the centre. The area of the quadrilateral TEKI is:
questions.solution:
Length of tangents $KE = KI = \sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{289 - 64} = 15\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area of quadrilateral TEKI} = 2 \times \text{Area}(\Delta\text{TEK}) = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 15\right) = 120\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: What will be the area of a plot of quadrilateral shape, one of whose diagonals is 20 m and lengths of the perpendiculars from the opposite vertices on it are 12 m and 18 m, respectively?
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times d \times (h_1 + h_2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times (12 + 18) = 10 \times 30 = 300\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: In $\Delta\text{PQR}$, M, N, and S are the mid-points of sides PQ, PR and QR, respectively. If the area of the $\Delta\text{PQR}$ is $46\text{ cm}^2$, what is the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the quadrilateral MNRQ?
questions.solution:
By midpoint theorem, $\Delta\text{PMN} \sim \Delta\text{PQR}$ with scale factor $\frac{1}{2}$, so $\text{Area}(\Delta\text{PMN}) = \frac{1}{4} \times 46 = 11.5\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{Area}(\text{quadrilateral MNRQ}) = \text{Area}(\Delta\text{PQR}) - \text{Area}(\Delta\text{PMN}) = 46 - 11.5 = 34.5\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: From a point A, which is at a distance of 17 cm from the centre C of a circle with radius 8 cm, the pair of tangents AB and AD to the circle are drawn. The area of the quadrilateral ABCD is ----- $\text{cm}^2$.
questions.solution:
Length of tangents $AB = AD = \sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = 15\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Area}(\text{quadrilateral ABCD}) = 2 \times \text{Area}(\Delta\text{ABC}) = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 15\right) = 120\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of a rectangle whose length is 52m and breadth is 9m.
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = l \times b = 52 \times 9 = 468\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is 70 cm and its diagonal is 25cm. The area of the rectangle is:
The area of a rectangular field is $3600\text{ m}^2$. If the field is 45 m long, what is its perimeter?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Breadth } b = \frac{3600}{45} = 80\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(l + b) = 2(45 + 80) = 2 \times 125 = 250\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a rectangular field is $480\text{ m}^2$. If the length is 20% more than the breadth, then the length of the rectangular field is:
questions.solution:
$$l = 1.2b = \frac{6}{5} b.$$
$$\text{Area} = l \times b = \frac{6}{5} b^2 = 480 \implies b^2 = 400 \implies b = 20\text{ m}.$$
$$l = 1.2 \times 20 = 24\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio of the length to width of a certain rectangle is $3:2$ and the area is $150\text{ cm}^2$. The perimeter of the rectangle (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = 3x \times 2x = 6x^2 = 150 \implies x^2 = 25 \implies x = 5.$$
$$l = 15\text{ cm}, \quad b = 10\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(l + b) = 2(15 + 10) = 50\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangular park is $3:2$, and the perimeter of the park is 120 m. Find the area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the park.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(3x + 2x) = 10x = 120 \implies x = 12.$$
$$l = 36\text{ m}, \quad b = 24\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area} = 36 \times 24 = 864\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: In a rectangular field, the sum of the length and the breadth is 9 cm and area is $18\text{ cm}^2$. If the length is 'a' and breadth is 'b', then find the value of $(a^2 - ab + b^2)$.
The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 48 m. If the length is 6 m more than the breadth, the area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the garden is?
questions.solution:
$$2(l + b) = 48 \implies l + b = 24, \quad l - b = 6.$$
$$l = 15\text{ m}, \quad b = 9\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area} = 15 \times 9 = 135\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The length of a rectangular shaped park exceeds its breadth by 15 m. If the perimeter of the park is 110 m, find the length of the park (in m).
questions.solution:
$$2(l + b) = 110 \implies l + b = 55, \quad l - b = 15.$$
$$2l = 70 \implies l = 35\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: If the semi-perimeter and area of a rectangular field whose length and breadth are '$x$' and '$y$' is 12 cm and $28\text{ cm}^2$, respectively, then find the value of $x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4$.
Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden, whose length is 8 cm more than its width, is 42 cm. Find the area of the rectangular garden.
questions.solution:
$$l + w = 42, \quad l - w = 8.$$
$$2l = 50 \implies l = 25\text{ cm}, \quad w = 17\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = l \times w = 25 \times 17 = 425\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The dimensions of a rectangular field when extended by 6 meters are in the ratio of $4:3$ and when decreased by 6 meters are in the ratio of $2:1$. Find the dimensions of the field
questions.solution:
$$\frac{l + 6}{b + 6} = \frac{4}{3} \implies 3l - 4b = 6.$$
$$\frac{l - 6}{b - 6} = \frac{2}{1} \implies l - 2b = -6 \implies 2l - 4b = -12.$$
Subtracting gives $l = 18\text{ meters}$.
$$18 - 2b = -6 \implies 2b = 24 \implies b = 12\text{ meters}.$$

questions.questionText: The width of a rectangle is 2 m less than its length. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 68 m, then what is the length (in m) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
$$2(l + b) = 68 \implies l + b = 34, \quad l - b = 2.$$
$$2l = 36 \implies l = 18\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: A field is 150 m long and 80 m wide. How many times (rounded off to 1 decimal place) is its perimeter to the length of its diagonal?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(150 + 80) = 460\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Diagonal} = \sqrt{150^2 + 80^2} = \sqrt{22500 + 6400} = \sqrt{28900} = 170\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{460}{170} \approx 2.7058 \approx 2.7.$$

questions.questionText: Half of the perimeter of a rectangle is 30 cm. If the length of the rectangle is 6 cm more than its breadth, then what is the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
$$l + b = 30, \quad l - b = 6.$$
$$2l = 36 \implies l = 18\text{ cm}, \quad b = 12\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = 18 \times 12 = 216\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The breadth of a rectangular floor is $\frac{3}{5}$ of its length. If the area of the floor is $60\text{ meter}^2$ then what is the difference between the length and breadth of the floor?
questions.solution:
$$b = \frac{3}{5} l.$$
$$\text{Area} = l \times \frac{3}{5} l = \frac{3}{5} l^2 = 60 \implies l^2 = 100 \implies l = 10\text{ m}.$$
$$b = 6\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Difference} = l - b = 10 - 6 = 4\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: If the length of certain rectangle is decreased by 4 cm and breadth is increased by 2 cm, it would result in a square of the same area. What is the perimeter of the original rectangle?
questions.solution:
Since it results in a square: $l - 4 = b + 2 \implies l - b = 6$.
Same area: $(l - 4)(b + 2) = lb \implies lb + 2l - 4b - 8 = lb \implies 2l - 4b = 8 \implies l - 2b = 4$.
Subtracting: $b = 2\text{ cm} \implies l = 8\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(l + b) = 2(8 + 2) = 20\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: If length of a rectangle becomes three times and breadth is decreased to its half, then the ratio of the area of given rectangle to the area of new rectangle is:
questions.solution:
Original area $A_1 = lb$.
New area $A_2 = (3l) \times \left(\frac{b}{2}\right) = \frac{3}{2} lb$.
$$\frac{A_1}{A_2} = \frac{lb}{\frac{3}{2} lb} = \frac{2}{3} = 2:3.$$

questions.questionText: The cost of tilling the floor of a rectangular room is ₹9100 at ₹$65\text{ per m}^2$. The ratio of the length and breadth of the floor is $7:5$. The perimeter (in m) of the floor of the room is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{9100}{65} = 140\text{ m}^2.$$
$$7x \times 5x = 35x^2 = 140 \implies x^2 = 4 \implies x = 2.$$
$$l = 14\text{ m}, \quad b = 10\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(14 + 10) = 48\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a triangular plot having sides 12 m, 35 m and 37 m is equal to the area of a rectangular field whose sides are in the ratio $7:3$. The perimeter (in m) of the field is:
questions.solution:
Since $12^2 + 35^2 = 144 + 1225 = 1369 = 37^2$, the triangle is right-angled.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 35 = 210\text{ m}^2.$$
$$7x \times 3x = 21x^2 = 210 \implies x^2 = 10 \implies x = \sqrt{10}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(7x + 3x) = 20x = 20\sqrt{10}\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a triangular field whose sides are 65m, 72, and 97m is equal to the area of a rectangular park whose sides are in the ratio of $5:13$. What is the perimeter (in m) of the rectangular park?
questions.solution:
Since $65^2 + 72^2 = 4225 + 5184 = 9409 = 97^2$, the triangle is right-angled.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 65 \times 72 = 2340\text{ m}^2.$$
$$5x \times 13x = 65x^2 = 2340 \implies x^2 = 36 \implies x = 6.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(5x + 13x) = 36x = 36 \times 6 = 216\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a triangular park with sides 88 m, 165 m, and 187 m is equal to the area of a rectangular plot whose sides are in the ratio $5:3$. What is the perimeter (in m) of the plot?
questions.solution:
Dividing the sides by 11 gives 8, 15, 17, which is a Pythagorean triplet ($8^2 + 15^2 = 17^2$). Thus $88^2 + 165^2 = 187^2$.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 88 \times 165 = 7260\text{ m}^2.$$
$$5x \times 3x = 15x^2 = 7260 \implies x^2 = 484 \implies x = 22.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(5x + 3x) = 16x = 16 \times 22 = 352\text{ m}.$$

questions.questionText: A rectangular courtyard is 4m 95cm long and 16m 65cm broad. It is to be paved with the square tiles of the same size. Find the least number of such square tiles required to pave the rectangular courtyard.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Length} = 495\text{ cm}, \quad \text{Breadth} = 1665\text{ cm}.$$
$$\gcd(495, 1665) = 45\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Least number of tiles} = \frac{495}{45} \times \frac{1665}{45} = 11 \times 37 = 407.$$

questions.questionText: A rectangular lawn whose length is twice of its breadth is extended by having four semi-circular portions on its sides. What is the total area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the lawn if the smaller side of the rectangle is 12 m? (Take $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Breadth} = 12\text{ m}, \quad \text{Length} = 24\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area of rectangle} = 24 \times 12 = 288\text{ m}^2.$$
Two semicircles on length sides (radius 12 m) form 1 circle of radius 12 m:
$$\text{Area}_1 = 3.14 \times 12^2 = 452.16\text{ m}^2.$$
Two semicircles on breadth sides (radius 6 m) form 1 circle of radius 6 m:
$$\text{Area}_2 = 3.14 \times 6^2 = 113.04\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Total area} = 288 + 452.16 + 113.04 = 853.2\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A rectangle with the largest area is cut out of a circle with radius 5 units. What is the area of the remaining portion?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area of circle} = \pi (5^2) = 25\pi.$$
The rectangle of largest area inscribed in a circle of radius $R = 5$ is a square with diagonal $2R = 10$.
$$\text{Area of square} = \frac{1}{2} d^2 = \frac{1}{2} (10^2) = 50.$$
$$\text{Remaining area} = 25\pi - 50 = 25(\pi - 2).$$

questions.questionText: The length and the breadth of the floor of a rectangular hall are 126 feet and 90 feet, respectively. What will be the area (in square feet) of each of the largest identical square tiles that can be used to tile this floor in a way that no part of the floor remains uncovered?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side of largest square tile} = \gcd(126, 90) = 18\text{ feet}.$$
$$\text{Area of each tile} = 18^2 = 324\text{ feet}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A path of uniform width 2.5 m runs around the outside of a rectangular field of dimensions $45\text{ m} \times 35\text{ m}$. What is the area of the path (in $\text{m}^2$)?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Outer dimensions} = (45 + 2 \times 2.5) \times (35 + 2 \times 2.5) = 50\text{ m} \times 40\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Outer area} = 50 \times 40 = 2000\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Inner area} = 45 \times 35 = 1575\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Area of path} = 2000 - 1575 = 425\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: There is a rectangular garden of $240\text{ meters} \times 80\text{ meters}$. A path of width 4 meter is build outside the garden along its four sides. What is the area of the path?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Outer dimensions} = (240 + 8) \times (80 + 8) = 248 \times 88 = 21824\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Inner area} = 240 \times 80 = 19200\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Area of path} = 21824 - 19200 = 2624\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: If the perimeter of a square is 64 cm, what would be its area?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side } a = \frac{64}{4} = 16\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = a^2 = 16^2 = 256\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of a square, one of whose diagonals is 4.8 m long.
The side of a square is 5 cm. If the side is doubled, by how many times will the area of the square increase?
questions.solution: Original area $A_1 = a^2$. When the side is doubled ($a' = 2a$), new area $A_2 = (2a)^2 = 4a^2 = 4A_1$. Thus the area becomes 4 times the original.

questions.questionText: The diagonal of the square is $8\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$. Find the diagonal of another square whose area is triple that of the first square.
A man walking at a speed of 3 km/h crosses a square field diagonally in 5 minutes. What is the area of the field (in $\text{m}^2$)?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Speed} = 3 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{5}{6}\text{ m/s}.$$
$$\text{Time} = 5 \times 60 = 300\text{ s}.$$
$$\text{Diagonal } d = \frac{5}{6} \times 300 = 250\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} d^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 250^2 = 31250\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The width of the path around a square field is 4.5 m and its area is $105.75\text{ m}^2$. Find the cost of fencing the field at the rate of ₹100 per meter.
questions.solution:
Let the side of the square field be $s$. Outer side $= s + 2(4.5) = s + 9$.
$$\text{Area of path} = (s + 9)^2 - s^2 = 18s + 81 = 105.75 \implies 18s = 24.75 \implies s = 1.375\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter of field} = 4s = 4 \times 1.375 = 5.5\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Cost of fencing} = 5.5 \times 100 = ₹550.$$

questions.questionText: Using the mid points of sides of a square with an area of 36 square units, another square is made. What is the area of a new square made (in square units)?
questions.solution:
The square formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of a square has area equal to half of the original square's area.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 36 = 18\text{ sq. units}.$$

questions.questionText: Nine times the area of a circle is same as the three times the area of a square. What is the ratio of the diameter of the circle and diagonal of the square?
questions.solution:
$$9 (\pi r^2) = 3 a^2 \implies a^2 = 3\pi r^2 \implies a = r\sqrt{3\pi}.$$
$$\text{Diagonal of square } D = a\sqrt{2} = r\sqrt{6\pi}.$$
$$\text{Diameter of circle } d = 2r.$$
$$\frac{d}{D} = \frac{2r}{r\sqrt{6\pi}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{6\pi}} = \frac{\sqrt{4}}{\sqrt{6\pi}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3\pi}} = \sqrt{2} : \sqrt{3\pi}.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a square whose area is the same as the area of a semi-circle of radius $2\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area of semicircle} = \frac{1}{2} \pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2} \pi (2\sqrt{2})^2 = \frac{1}{2} \pi (8) = 4\pi.$$
$$\text{Area of square } a^2 = 4\pi \implies a = 2\sqrt{\pi}\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter} = 4a = 4(2\sqrt{\pi}) = 8\sqrt{\pi}\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle is equal to the perimeter of a square. If the length and the breadth of the rectangle are 10 cm and 8 cm respectively, then what will be the area of the square?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(10 + 8) = 36\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Side of square } a = \frac{36}{4} = 9\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area} = a^2 = 9^2 = 81\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a square is S, and that of the square formed by joining the mid-points of the given square is A. The value of $\frac{A}{S}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The square formed by connecting the midpoints of the sides of a square has area $A = \frac{S}{2}$.
$$\frac{A}{S} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5.$$

questions.questionText: Find the area of a circle whose radius is equal to the side of a square whose perimeter is 196 m.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side of square } a = \frac{196}{4} = 49\text{ m} = r.$$
$$\text{Area of circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 49^2 = 22 \times 7 \times 49 = 7546\text{ m}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a triangle is half the area of a square. The perimeter of the square is 172cm. What is the area of the triangle (in $\text{cm}^2$)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side of square } a = \frac{172}{4} = 43\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of square} = 43^2 = 1849\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Area of triangle} = \frac{1849}{2} = 924.5\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a square is $1156\text{ cm}^2$. What is the respective ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangle whose length is twice the side of the square and whose breadth is 14 cm less than the side of the square?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side of square } a = \sqrt{1156} = 34\text{ cm}.$$
$$l = 2 \times 34 = 68\text{ cm}, \quad b = 34 - 14 = 20\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{68}{20} = \frac{17}{5} = 17:5.$$

questions.questionText: The length of each side of a square is twice the radius of a circle. If the radius of the circle is 7 cm, then what is the difference between the areas of the square and the circle? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$r = 7\text{ cm} \implies a = 2r = 14\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of square} = 14^2 = 196\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Area of circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 = 154\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Difference} = 196 - 154 = 42\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: Each side of a square is 12 cm long. The perimeter of this square is equal to the perimeter of a rectangle whose length is 16 cm. What will be the area of this rectangle?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times 12 = 48\text{ cm}.$$
$$2(16 + b) = 48 \implies 16 + b = 24 \implies b = 8\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of rectangle} = 16 \times 8 = 128\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: What is the area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of a circle inscribed in a square of area $784\text{ cm}^2$? [Take $\pi = 22/7$]
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side of square } a = \sqrt{784} = 28\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Radius of inscribed circle } r = \frac{a}{2} = 14\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 22 \times 28 = 616\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The area of a square shaped field is $1764\text{ m}^2$. The breadth of a rectangular park is $\frac{1}{3}\text{rd}$ the side of the square field and its length is two times its breadth. What is the cost (in ₹) of leveling the park at ₹15 per $\text{m}^2$?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Side of square } a = \sqrt{1764} = 42\text{ m}.$$
$$b = \frac{42}{3} = 14\text{ m}, \quad l = 2 \times 14 = 28\text{ m}.$$
$$\text{Area of park} = 28 \times 14 = 392\text{ m}^2.$$
$$\text{Cost} = 392 \times 15 = ₹5880.$$

questions.questionText: A square has the perimeter equal to the circumference of a circle having radius 7 cm. What is the ratio of the area of the circle to area of the square?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Circumference} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 44\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Perimeter of square} = 4a = 44 \implies a = 11\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of circle} = \frac{22}{7} \times 49 = 154\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Area of square} = 11^2 = 121\text{ cm}^2.$$
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{154}{121} = \frac{14}{11} = 14:11.$$

questions.questionText: The base of a triangle is equal to the perimeter of a square whose diagonal is $7\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ and its height is equal to the side of a square whose area is $169\text{ m}^2$. The area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Diagonal} = 7\sqrt{2}\text{ cm} \implies \text{side } a = 7\text{ cm} \implies \text{base } b = 4 \times 7 = 28\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Height } h = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of triangle} = \frac{1}{2} \times 28 \times 13 = 182\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The base of a triangle is equal to the perimeter of a square whose diagonal is $6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$, and its height is equal to the side of a square whose area is $144\text{ cm}^2$. The area of the triangle (in $\text{cm}^2$) is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Diagonal} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm} \implies \text{side } a = 6\text{ cm} \implies \text{base } b = 4 \times 6 = 24\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Height } h = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}.$$
$$\text{Area of triangle} = \frac{1}{2} \times 24 \times 12 = 144\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: A wire is in the form of square with side 11 cm. It is bent to form a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter of square} = 4 \times 11 = 44\text{ cm}.$$
$$2\pi r = 44 \implies 2 \times \frac{22}{7} r = 44 \implies r = 7\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The diagonal of a square A is $(a + b)$ units. What will be the area (in square units) of the square drawn on the diagonal of square B, whose area is twice the area of square A?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Area of square A} = \frac{1}{2} d_A^2 = \frac{1}{2} (a + b)^2.$$
$$\text{Area of square B} = 2 \times \text{Area of A} = (a + b)^2.$$
The area of the square drawn on the diagonal of square B is $d_B^2 = 2 \times \text{Area of B} = 2(a + b)^2$.

questions.questionText: The area of a parallelogram with base 26 cm and height 18 cm is:
questions.solution: $$\text{Area} = \text{base} \times \text{height} = 26 \times 18 = 468\text{ cm}^2.$$

questions.questionText: The base of a parallelogram is twice its height. If the area of the parallelogram is $338\text{ cm}^2$, then find its height (in cm).
questions.solution:
$$b = 2h.$$
$$\text{Area} = b \times h = 2h^2 = 338 \implies h^2 = 169 \implies h = 13\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The base of a parallelogram is thrice its height. If the area of the parallelogram is $1020\text{ cm}^2$, then what is its height?
questions.solution:
$$b = 3h.$$
$$\text{Area} = b \times h = 3h^2 = 1020 \implies h^2 = 340 \implies h = \sqrt{340} = 2\sqrt{85}\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a parallelogram is 48 cm. If the height of the parallelogram is 6 cm and the length of the adjacent side is 8 cm. find its area.
questions.solution:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 2(a + b) = 48 \implies a + b = 24.$$
