Given $r = 3.5 = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}$ and $h = 18\text{ cm}$:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2 \times 18 = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{49}{4} \times 18 = \frac{11 \times 7 \times 6}{2} = 231\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: If the height of a cone is $7\text{ cm}$ and the diameter of the circular base is $12\text{ cm}$, then its volume is (nearest to integer):
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 12\text{ cm} \implies r = 6\text{ cm}$. Height $h = 7\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 6^2 \times 7 = \frac{1}{3} \times 22 \times 36 = 22 \times 12 = 264\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: What is the volume of a cone (in cubic units) with radius $3\text{ units}$ and slant height $3\sqrt{2}\text{ units}$?
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 3$, slant height $l = 3\sqrt{2}$.
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{(3\sqrt{2})^2 - 3^2} = \sqrt{18 - 9} = \sqrt{9} = 3\text{ units}$.
Volume:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \pi (3^2)(3) = 9\pi$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: What is the height (in $\text{m}$) of a conical water tank having radius of $70\text{ m}$ and volume of $46,200\text{ m}^3$? $\left(\text{Take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = 46200$.
$$\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 70 \times 70 \times h = 46200$$
$$\frac{1}{3} \times 22 \times 10 \times 70 \times h = 46200$$
$$\frac{15400}{3} h = 46200 \implies h = \frac{46200 \times 3}{15400} = 3 \times 3 = 9\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: If the height of a right circular cone is $24\text{ cm}$ and radius of its base is $10.5\text{ cm}$, then the volume of right circular cone (in $\text{cm}^3$) is: $\left(\text{Take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Height $h = 24\text{ cm}$, radius $r = 10.5 = \frac{21}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{21}{2}\right)^2 \times 24 = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{441}{4} \times 24 = 22 \times 21 \times 6 = 2772\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the radius of the base and slant height of the cone is $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$, respectively, then the volume of the cone is equal to:
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$, slant height $l = 10\text{ cm}$.
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ cm}$.
Volume:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \pi (6^2)(8) = \frac{1}{3} \pi (36)(8) = 96\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The volume of a right circular cone is $150\pi\text{ cm}^3$ and its height is $18\text{ cm}$. Find its slant height (in $\text{cm}$) (correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = 150\pi$.
$$\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 (18) = 150\pi \implies 6 r^2 = 150 \implies r^2 = 25 \implies r = 5\text{ cm}$$
Slant height $l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 18^2} = \sqrt{25 + 324} = \sqrt{349} \approx 18.68\text{ cm}$.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The height and radius of a cone-shaped storage tank are $9\text{ ft.}$ and $7\text{ft.}$, respectively. Find the volume of water the tank can hold? $\left[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7\right]$
questions.solution:
Height $h = 9\text{ ft}$, radius $r = 7\text{ ft}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times 9 = 22 \times 7 \times 3 = 462\text{ cubic fit}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is $20\pi\text{ cm}^2$. If its radius is $4\text{ cm}$, then find the volume of cone
questions.solution:
Curved surface area $\text{CSA} = \pi r l = 20\pi$.
Given $r = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$4\pi l = 20\pi \implies l = 5\text{ cm}$$
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{5^2 - 4^2} = 3\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \pi (4^2)(3) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: Volume of a cone whose radius of base and height are $r$ and $h$ respectively, is $400\text{ cm}^3$. What will be the volume of a cone whose radius of base and height are $2r\text{ cm}$ and $h\text{ cm}$ respectively?
questions.solution:
Initial volume $V_1 = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = 400\text{ cm}^3$.
New cone has radius $R = 2r$ and height $H = h$.
New volume:
$$V_2 = \frac{1}{3} \pi (2r)^2 h = 4 \times \left(\frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h\right) = 4 \times 400 = 1600\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The volume of a right circular cone having a base diameter of $14\text{ cm}$ is $196\pi\text{ cm}^3$. Find the perpendicular height of this cone
questions.solution:
Base diameter $= 14\text{ cm} \implies r = 7\text{ cm}$.
Volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = 196\pi$:
$$\frac{1}{3} \pi (7^2) h = 196\pi \implies \frac{49}{3} h = 196 \implies h = \frac{196 \times 3}{49} = 4 \times 3 = 12\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The radius of the base of a right circular cone is $5\text{ cm}$. Its slant height is $13\text{ cm}$. What is its volume (in $\text{cm}^3$, rounded off to 1 decimal place)? $\left[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7\right]$
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$, slant height $l = 13\text{ cm}$.
Height $h = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\text{ cm}$.
Volume:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 5^2 \times 12 = \frac{2200}{7} \approx 314.3\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The height and the radius of the base of a right circular cone are in the ratio of $12: 5$. If its volume is $314\text{ cm}^3$, then what is the slant height of the cone? (Use $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
Let height $h = 12x$ and radius $r = 5x$.
Slant height $l = \sqrt{h^2 + r^2} = \sqrt{(12x)^2 + (5x)^2} = 13x$.
Volume $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = 314$:
$$\frac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times (5x)^2 \times (12x) = 314$$
$$3.14 \times 100 x^3 = 314 \implies x = 1$$
Therefore, slant height $l = 13(1) = 13\text{ cm}$.
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A conical tent is set to accommodate $15\text{ persons}$. Each person must have $5\text{ square meters}$ of space on the ground and $30\text{ cubic meters}$ of air to breathe. What is the height of the cone?
questions.solution:
Ground space required (base area $B$) $= 15 \times 5 = 75\text{ m}^2$.
Total volume of air required $V = 15 \times 30 = 450\text{ m}^3$.
Volume of a cone is given by:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{Base Area} \times h$$
$$450 = \frac{1}{3} \times 75 \times h = 25 h \implies h = 18\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: If the diameter of the base of a cone is $70\text{ cm}$ and its curved surface area is $4070\text{ cm}^2$, then what will be its volume (in $\text{cm}^3$)? $\left[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7\right]$
questions.solution:
Base diameter $= 70\text{ cm} \implies r = 35\text{ cm}$.
Curved surface area $\text{CSA} = \pi r l = 4070$:
$$\frac{22}{7} \times 35 \times l = 4070 \implies 110 l = 4070 \implies l = 37\text{ cm}$$
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{37^2 - 35^2} = \sqrt{(37 - 35)(37 + 35)} = \sqrt{2 \times 72} = 12\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 35^2 \times 12 = 15400\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If a right circular cone of height $24\text{ cm}$ has the circumference of its base $42\pi\text{ cm}$, then the volume of the cone is $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$.
questions.solution:
Circumference of base $2\pi r = 42\pi \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$.
Height $h = 24\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 \times 24 = 22 \times 3 \times 21 \times 8 = 11088\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The volume of a cone with height equal to radius, and slant height $5\text{ cm}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $h = r$, so slant height $l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{2r^2} = r\sqrt{2} = 5 \implies r = \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^3 = \frac{125\pi}{3 \times 2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{125\pi}{6\sqrt{2}}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A conical vessel (solid) is made of iron. Its base radius is $7\text{ cm}$ and height is $15\text{ cm}$. If the weight of iron per cubic centimeter is $15\text{ g}$, what is the weight of the vessel?
questions.solution:
Volume of conical vessel:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times 15 = 22 \times 7 \times 5 = 770\text{ cm}^3$$
Weight of the vessel:
$$\text{Weight} = 770 \times 15\text{ g} = 11550\text{ g} = 11.55\text{ kg}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A conical vessel has radius $4\text{ cm}$ and its curved surface area is $20\pi\text{ cm}^2$. The volume of conical vessel is:
questions.solution:
Curved surface area $\pi r l = 20\pi$.
Given $r = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$4\pi l = 20\pi \implies l = 5\text{ cm}$$
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{5^2 - 4^2} = 3\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the conical vessel:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (4^2)(3) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The heights of two right circular cones are in the ratio $1 : 5$ and the perimeter of their bases are in the ratio $5 : 3$. Find the ratio of their volumes.
questions.solution:
Let the ratio of radii be $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{5}{3}$ (since ratio of perimeters equals ratio of radii).
Ratio of heights $\frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{1}{5}$.
Ratio of volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{\frac{1}{3}\pi r_1^2 h_1}{\frac{1}{3}\pi r_2^2 h_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2 \left(\frac{h_1}{h_2}\right) = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 \left(\frac{1}{5}\right) = \frac{25}{9} \times \frac{1}{5} = \frac{5}{9}$$
Hence, the ratio is $5 : 9$, option C.

questions.questionText: The radii of the two cones are in the ratio of $2 : 5$ and their volumes are in the ratio of $3 : 5$. What is the ratio of their heights?
questions.solution:
Ratio of volumes $\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2 \left(\frac{h_1}{h_2}\right)$.
Given $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{2}{5}$ and $\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{3}{5}$:
$$\frac{3}{5} = \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 \left(\frac{h_1}{h_2}\right) = \frac{4}{25} \left(\frac{h_1}{h_2}\right)$$
$$\frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{25}{4} = \frac{15}{4}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: If the radius of the right circular cone is increased by $20\%$ and its height is decreased by $25\%$, then the volume of the right circular cone will be increased by:
questions.solution:
Volume $V \propto r^2 h$.
Let initial $r = 1$ and $h = 1$, so initial $V = 1$.
New radius $r' = 1 + 0.20 = 1.20$.
New height $h' = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75$.
New volume $V' = (1.20)^2 \times 0.75 = 1.44 \times 0.75 = 1.08$.
Percentage increase in volume $= (1.08 - 1) \times 100\% = 8\%$.
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the ratio of the volumes of two cones is 11:16 and the ratio of the radii of their bases is 3:4, then the ratio of their heights will be:
questions.solution:
Given $\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{11}{16}$ and $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{3}{4}$.
Since $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2 \times \frac{h_1}{h_2}$$
$$\frac{11}{16} = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 \times \frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{9}{16} \times \frac{h_1}{h_2}$$
$$\frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{11}{9}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The slant height and radius of a right circular cone are in the ratio 29:20. If its volume is $4838.4\pi\text{ cm}^3$, then its radius is:
questions.solution:
Let slant height $l = 29x$ and radius $r = 20x$.
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{(29x)^2 - (20x)^2} = \sqrt{841x^2 - 400x^2} = \sqrt{441x^2} = 21x$.
Volume of cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (20x)^2 (21x) = 2800\pi x^3$$
Given $V = 4838.4\pi\text{ cm}^3$:
$$2800\pi x^3 = 4838.4\pi \implies x^3 = \frac{4838.4}{2800} = 1.728 = (1.2)^3 \implies x = 1.2$$
Therefore, radius $r = 20x = 20 \times 1.2 = 24\text{ cm}$.
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: If the diameter of the base of a cone is $56\text{ cm}$ and its curved surface area is $3080\text{ cm}^2$, then what will be its volume (in $\text{cm}^3$)? $(\text{Use } \pi = 22/7)$
questions.solution:
Base diameter $= 56\text{ cm} \implies r = 28\text{ cm}$.
Curved surface area $\text{CSA} = \pi r l = 3080$:
$$\frac{22}{7} \times 28 \times l = 3080 \implies 88 l = 3080 \implies l = 35\text{ cm}$$
Height $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{35^2 - 28^2} = 7\sqrt{5^2 - 4^2} = 7 \times 3 = 21\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 28^2 \times 21 = 22 \times 784 = 17248\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: Find the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$, rounded off to 2 decimal places) of a right circular cone of diameter $12\text{ cm}$ and height $5\text{ cm}$. $[\text{Use } \pi = \frac{22}{7}]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 12\text{ cm} \implies r = 6\text{ cm}$, height $h = 5\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 6^2 \times 5 = \frac{22 \times 12 \times 5}{7} = \frac{1320}{7} \approx 188.57\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The height of a right circular cone is $63\text{ cm}$ and the area of its curved surface is five times the area of its base. What is the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of the cone? $(\text{Use } \pi = \frac{22}{7})$
questions.solution:
Given $\text{CSA} = 5 \times \text{Base Area} \implies \pi r l = 5 \pi r^2 \implies l = 5r$.
Since $h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{25r^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{24}r = 2\sqrt{6}r = 63$:
$$r = \frac{63}{2\sqrt{6}} \implies r^2 = \frac{3969}{24} = \frac{1323}{8}$$
Volume of cone:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{1323}{8} \times 63 = \frac{22 \times 63 \times 63}{8} = 10914.75\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A toy is in the form of a cone mounted on a hemisphere. The radius of the hemisphere and that of the cone is $36\text{ cm}$ and height of the cone is $105\text{ cm}$. The total surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the toy is:
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 36\text{ cm}$, cone height $h = 105\text{ cm}$.
Slant height $l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{36^2 + 105^2} = 3\sqrt{12^2 + 35^2} = 3 \times 37 = 111\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area of the toy:
$$\text{TSA} = \text{CSA of cone} + \text{CSA of hemisphere} = \pi r l + 2\pi r^2 = \pi r (l + 2r)$$
$$\text{TSA} = \pi \times 36 \times (111 + 72) = 36 \times 183 \times \pi = 6588\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: A $22.5\text{ m}$ high tent is in the shape of a frustum of a cone surmounted by a hemisphere. If the diameters of the upper and the lower circular ends of the frustum are $21\text{ m}$ and $39\text{m}$, respectively, then find the area of the cloth (in $\text{m}^2$) used to make the tent (ignoring the wastage). $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Upper radius $r_1 = \frac{21}{2} = 10.5\text{ m}$, lower radius $r_2 = \frac{39}{2} = 19.5\text{ m}$.
Since the hemisphere surmounts the upper end, its radius is $r = 10.5\text{ m}$ and height is $10.5\text{ m}$.
Height of the frustum $h = 22.5 - 10.5 = 12\text{ m}$.
Slant height of frustum $l = \sqrt{h^2 + (r_2 - r_1)^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + (19.5 - 10.5)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 81} = 15\text{ m}$.
Area of cloth = CSA of frustum + CSA of hemisphere:
$$\text{Area} = \pi (r_1 + r_2) l + 2\pi r_1^2 = \pi (30 \times 15 + 2 \times 110.25) = \pi (450 + 220.5) = 670.5\pi$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times 670.5 = \frac{14751}{7} = 2107\frac{2}{7}\text{ m}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The radii of the ends of a frustum of a cone $7\text{ cm}$ height are $5\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$. Find its volume correct to one decimal place. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Given radii $R = 5\text{ cm}$, $r = 3\text{ cm}$, and height $h = 7\text{ cm}$.
Volume of frustum:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi h (R^2 + r^2 + Rr) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times (5^2 + 3^2 + 5 \times 3) = \frac{22}{3} \times (25 + 9 + 15) = \frac{22 \times 49}{3} = \frac{1078}{3} \approx 359.3\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: Find the surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of a sphere of diameter $28\text{ cm}$. $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 28\text{ cm} \implies r = 14\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of sphere:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 28 = 2464\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of a sphere, whose diameter is $42\text{ cm}$, is: $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 42\text{ cm} \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of sphere:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 63 = 5544\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: Find the surface area of a ball of radius $21\text{ mm}$. $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 21\text{ mm}$.
Surface area of the ball:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 63 = 5544\text{ mm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: If the surface area of the sphere is $616\text{ cm}^2$, then the radius of the sphere is equal to:
questions.solution:
Surface area of sphere $= 4\pi r^2 = 616$:
$$4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 = 616 \implies \frac{88}{7} r^2 = 616 \implies r^2 = 616 \times \frac{7}{88} = 49 \implies r = 7.0\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the radius of a sphere is increased by $40\%$, then find the percentage increase in its surface area.
questions.solution:
Surface area of a sphere $\text{SA} \propto r^2$.
If radius increases by $40\%$, the new radius is $1.4r$.
New surface area $\propto (1.4)^2 = 1.96$.
Percentage increase $= (1.96 - 1) \times 100\% = 96\%$.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: If the radius of a sphere is increased by $125\%$, then by what percentage will its surface area increase (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
Surface area $\text{SA} \propto r^2$.
New radius $r' = r + 1.25r = 2.25r$.
New surface area $\propto (2.25)^2 = 5.0625$.
Percentage increase $= (5.0625 - 1) \times 100\% = 406.25\%$.
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: If the radius of a sphere is increased by $3.5\text{ cm}$, its surface area increases by $550\text{ cm}^2$. What was the original radius of the sphere? $\left(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Let original radius be $r$.
$$4\pi(r + 3.5)^2 - 4\pi r^2 = 550$$
$$4\pi ((r + 3.5)^2 - r^2) = 550$$
$$4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times (2r + 3.5)(3.5) = 550$$
$$44 \times (2r + 3.5) = 550 \implies 2r + 3.5 = 12.5 \implies 2r = 9 \implies r = 4.5\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: Rajesh is playing with football having diameter of $28\text{ cm}$. He wants to get a photo of his favourite player painted on the entire ball. The painter charges ₹$2/\text{cm}^2$. What will be the cost (in ₹) of painting the ball $\left(\text{take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$?
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 28\text{ cm} \implies r = 14\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of the ball:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 28 = 2464\text{ cm}^2$$
Total cost at ₹$2$ per $\text{cm}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 2464 \times 2 = ₹4928$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The outer surface of a sphere having diameter $10\text{ m}$ is painted at the rate of $\text{Rs. } \frac{80}{\pi}\text{ per }\text{m}^2$. What is the cost of painting?
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 10\text{ m} \implies r = 5\text{ m}$.
Surface area of sphere:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4\pi (5^2) = 100\pi\text{ m}^2$$
Cost of painting at Rs. $\frac{80}{\pi}$ per $\text{m}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 100\pi \times \frac{80}{\pi} = \text{Rs. } 8000$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: Find the cost of painting a ball that is in the shape of a sphere with a radius of $14\text{ cm}$. The painting cost of the ball is $\text{Rs.} 5\text{ per square centimetre }\left(\text{take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 14\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of sphere:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 28 = 2464\text{ cm}^2$$
Cost of painting at Rs. 5 per $\text{cm}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 2464 \times 5 = \text{Rs. } 12320$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The cost of painting a spherical vessel of diameter $14\text{ cm}$ is ₹$21,560$. What is the cost of painting (in ₹) per square centimeter? $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 14\text{ cm} \implies r = 7\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of spherical vessel:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 = 616\text{ cm}^2$$
Cost of painting per $\text{cm}^2$:
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{21560}{616} = ₹35$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: Aman wants to get his spherical overhead water tank having a diameter of $7\text{ m}$, painted. If the cost of painting is ₹$13\text{ per square meter}$. Find the cost of painting Aman's spherical overhead water tank. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 7\text{ m} \implies r = 3.5\text{ m} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ m}$.
Surface area of the spherical tank:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2 = 154\text{ m}^2$$
Cost of painting at ₹$13$ per $\text{m}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 154 \times 13 = ₹2002$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A spherical ball of diameter $8\text{ cm}$ is cut into two equal parts. The curved area of one such part has to be painted with green color, while the other part has to be painted with red color. The bases of both the hemispheres are to be painted with blue color. The cost of painting with blue is ₹$2/\text{cm}^2$, while the cost of painting the curved area is ₹$3/\text{cm}^2$. What will be the cost (in ₹) of painting the hemispheres? $(\text{Take } \pi = 3.14)$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 8\text{ cm} \implies r = 4\text{ cm}$.
Total curved surface area of both hemispheres $= 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r^2 = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times 3.14 \times 16 = 200.96\text{ cm}^2$.
Cost of painting curved areas at ₹$3/\text{cm}^2$:
$$\text{Curved Area Cost} = 200.96 \times 3 = ₹602.88$$
Total base area of both hemispheres $= 2 \times \pi r^2 = 2 \times 3.14 \times 16 = 100.48\text{ cm}^2$.
Cost of painting base areas at ₹$2/\text{cm}^2$:
$$\text{Base Area Cost} = 100.48 \times 2 = ₹200.96$$
Total cost $= 602.88 + 200.96 = ₹803.84$.
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the radius of a sphere is $2.1\text{ cm}$, then the volume of sphere is equal to:
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 2.1\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the sphere:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (2.1)^3 = \frac{88}{21} \times 9.261 = 88 \times 0.441 = 38.808\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: What is the radius of a sphere having a volume of $38808\text{ cm}^3$? $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 38808$:
$$\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^3 = 38808$$
$$\frac{88}{21} r^3 = 38808 \implies r^3 = 38808 \times \frac{21}{88} = 441 \times 21 = 9261 = 21^3 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: If the volume of a sphere is $972\pi\text{cm}^3$, then find its radius.
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 972\pi$:
$$\frac{4}{3} r^3 = 972 \implies r^3 = 972 \times \frac{3}{4} = 243 \times 3 = 729 = 9^3 \implies r = 9\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: Find the diameter of a spherical ball whose volume is $38.808\text{ cm}^3$. $\left(\text{Use } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 38.808$:
$$\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^3 = 38.808 \implies r^3 = 38.808 \times \frac{21}{88} = 9.261 = (2.1)^3 \implies r = 2.1\text{ cm}$$
Diameter $d = 2r = 2 \times 2.1 = 4.2\text{ cm}$.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The surface area of a sphere is $2464\text{ cm}^2$. Find its volume.
questions.solution:
Surface area $= 4\pi r^2 = 2464$:
$$4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 = 2464 \implies r^2 = 2464 \times \frac{7}{88} = 196 \implies r = 14\text{ cm}$$
Volume of the sphere:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^3 = \frac{88 \times 2 \times 196}{3} = \frac{34496}{3} = 11498\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the diameter of a sphere is reduced to its half, then the volume would be:

options.label: A
options.text: reduced by $\frac{1}{8}$ of the former volume

options.label: B
options.text: increased by $\frac{1}{4}$ of the former volume

options.label: C
options.text: reduced by $\frac{1}{4}$ of the former volume

options.label: D
options.text: increased by $\frac{1}{8}$ of the former volume

questions.solution:
Volume of a sphere $V \propto d^3$.
When the diameter is reduced to half, $d' = \frac{d}{2}$:
$$V' = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 V = \frac{1}{8}V$$
Thus, the volume becomes $\frac{1}{8}$ of the former volume (marked as option A in the official exam key).
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The radii of two spheres are in the ratio $4 : 5$. What will be the ratio of their volumes.
questions.solution:
Ratio of volumes of two spheres is equal to the ratio of the cubes of their radii:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^3 = \frac{64}{125}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The surface areas of two spheres are in the ratio $25 : 36$. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.solution:
Ratio of surface areas $\frac{S_1}{S_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{36} \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{5}{6}$.
Ratio of their volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^3 = \frac{125}{216}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: If the surface areas of two spheres are in the ratio of $49 : 81$, then find the ratio of their volumes.
questions.solution:
Ratio of surface areas $\frac{S_1}{S_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{81} \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{7}{9}$.
Ratio of their volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{7}{9}\right)^3 = \frac{343}{729}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The surface area of spherical ball is $1386\text{ cm}^2$. What will be its volume?
questions.solution:
Surface area of sphere $= 4\pi r^2 = 1386$:
$$4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 = 1386 \implies r^2 = 1386 \times \frac{7}{88} = \frac{441}{4} \implies r = \frac{21}{2}\text{ cm}$$
Volume of the sphere:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{21}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{88}{21} \times \frac{9261}{8} = 4851\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the surface areas of two spheres are in the ratio of $9 : 49$, then the ratio of their volumes is: $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Ratio of radii $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{49}} = \frac{3}{7}$.
Ratio of volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{3}{7}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{343}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The surface area of a sphere is $2464\text{ cm}^2$. Calculate its volume. $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Surface area $= 4\pi r^2 = 2464 \implies 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 = 2464 \implies r^2 = 196 \implies r = 14\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the sphere:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^3 = \frac{34496}{3} \approx 11498.67\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: Two metallic balls P and Q are such that the diameter of P is four times the diameter of Q. What is the ratio between the volumes of P and Q?
questions.solution:
Ratio of diameters $\frac{d_P}{d_Q} = 4$.
Ratio of volumes:
$$\frac{V_P}{V_Q} = \left(\frac{d_P}{d_Q}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64 = 64 : 1$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: As air is pumped into a spherical balloon, its radius increases from $7\text{ cm}$ to $14\text{ cm}$. Find the ratio of volume of the balloon's in both circumstances.
questions.solution:
Ratio of radii $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{7}{14} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Ratio of volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8} = 1 : 8$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The volumes of two spheres are in the ratio of $512 : 3375$. The ratio of their surface areas is:
questions.solution:
Ratio of volumes $\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{512}{3375} \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{512}{3375}} = \frac{8}{15}$.
Ratio of surface areas:
$$\frac{S_1}{S_2} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{8}{15}\right)^2 = \frac{64}{225}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: Find the total surface area of a sphere whose volume is $\frac{256}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{256}{3}\pi \implies 4r^3 = 256 \implies r^3 = 64 \implies r = 4\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of the sphere:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4\pi (4^2) = 64\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The volume of a sphere is given by $130977\text{ cm}^3$. Its surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) is:
questions.solution:
Volume of sphere $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 130977$:
$$\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^3 = 130977 \implies r^3 = 130977 \times \frac{21}{88} = 31255.875 = (31.5)^3 \implies r = 31.5\text{ cm}$$
Surface area:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times (31.5)^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 992.25 = 12474\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: If the volume of a sphere is $38808\text{ cm}^3$, then its surface area is:
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 38808 \implies r^3 = 9261 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$.
Surface area:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 63 = 5544\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: If the volume of a sphere is $24,416.64\text{ cm}^3$, find its surface area (take $\pi = 3.14$) correct to two places of decimal.
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 24416.64$:
$$\frac{4}{3} \times 3.14 \times r^3 = 24416.64 \implies r^3 = \frac{24416.64 \times 3}{12.56} = 5832 = 18^3 \implies r = 18\text{ cm}$$
Surface area:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times 3.14 \times 18^2 = 12.56 \times 324 = 4069.44\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: Let $x\text{ cm}^2$ be the surface area and $y\text{ cm}^3$ be the volume of a sphere such that $y = 14x$. What is the radius (in $\text{cm}$) of the sphere?
questions.solution:
Given $x = 4\pi r^2$ and $y = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
Given $y = 14x$:
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 14(4\pi r^2) \implies \frac{r}{3} = 14 \implies r = 42\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the total surface area and volume of a sphere is $2 : 7$. Its radius is:
questions.solution:
Ratio of surface area to volume:
$$\frac{4\pi r^2}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3} = \frac{3}{r} = \frac{2}{7} \implies 2r = 21 \implies r = 10.5\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The volumes of spheres A and B are in the ratio $125 : 64$. If the sum of the radii of A and B is $36\text{ cm}$, then what is the surface area (in sq. cm) of A?
questions.solution:
Ratio of volumes $\frac{V_A}{V_B} = \frac{125}{64} \implies \frac{r_A}{r_B} = \frac{5}{4}$.
Let $r_A = 5k$ and $r_B = 4k$.
Given $r_A + r_B = 9k = 36 \implies k = 4$.
Thus, $r_A = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of A:
$$\text{SA} = 4\pi r_A^2 = 4\pi (20^2) = 1600\pi\text{ sq. cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: A sphere and a cube have equal surface areas. The ratio of the volume of the sphere to that of the cube is:
questions.solution:
Given $4\pi r^2 = 6a^2 \implies \frac{r^2}{a^2} = \frac{6}{4\pi} = \frac{3}{2\pi} \implies \frac{r}{a} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2\pi}}$.
Ratio of their volumes:
$$\frac{V_{sphere}}{V_{cube}} = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3}{a^3} = \frac{4\pi}{3} \left(\frac{r}{a}\right)^3 = \frac{4\pi}{3} \times \left(\frac{3}{2\pi}\right) \sqrt{\frac{3}{2\pi}} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{3}{2\pi}} = \sqrt{\frac{12}{2\pi}} = \sqrt{\frac{6}{\pi}} = \sqrt{6} : \sqrt{\pi}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: What is the difference in the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of a sphere of radius $7\text{cm}$ and that of a cone of radius $7\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Volume of sphere $V_s = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^3 = \frac{4312}{3}\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of cone $V_c = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times 10 = \frac{1540}{3}\text{ cm}^3$.
Difference:
$$V_s - V_c = \frac{4312 - 1540}{3} = \frac{2772}{3} = 924\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: Find the number of paper balls, each $2\text{ cm}$ in diameter, that can be made from a sphere of diameter $18\text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
Number of balls $n = \frac{\text{Volume of large sphere}}{\text{Volume of small sphere}} = \left(\frac{D}{d}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{18}{2}\right)^3 = 9^3 = 729$.
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The sum of the radii of spheres A and B is $14\text{ cm}$, the radius of A being larger than that of B. The difference between their surface area is $112\pi$. What is the ratio of volumes of A and B?
questions.solution:
Given $r_A + r_B = 14$.
Difference between surface areas: $4\pi (r_A^2 - r_B^2) = 112\pi \implies r_A^2 - r_B^2 = 28$.
Since $r_A^2 - r_B^2 = (r_A + r_B)(r_A - r_B) = 28$:
$$14(r_A - r_B) = 28 \implies r_A - r_B = 2$$
Solving $r_A + r_B = 14$ and $r_A - r_B = 2$ gives $r_A = 8\text{ cm}$ and $r_B = 6\text{ cm}$.
Ratio of their volumes:
$$\frac{V_A}{V_B} = \left(\frac{r_A}{r_B}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{8}{6}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{64}{27} = 64 : 27$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: One laddoo with a radius of $5\text{ cm}$ belongs to a shopkeeper. How many laddoo of radius $2.5\text{ cm}$ may be created from the same one laddoo?
questions.solution:
Number of laddoos $n = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{5}{2.5}\right)^3 = 2^3 = 8$.
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper usually makes a large gram flour laddu (circular in shape) of radius $9\text{ cm}$. How many gram flour laddus of radius $3\text{ cm}$ can be made from this big gram flour laddu? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Number of small laddus $n = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{9}{3}\right)^3 = 3^3 = 27$.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The radius of the hollow sphere is $21\text{ cm}$. It is cut into two equal halves by a plane passing through its center. What is $75\%$ of the curved surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$, rounded off to the nearest tens) of the hemispheres? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Curved surface area of one hemisphere $= 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 = 44 \times 63 = 2772\text{ cm}^2$.
$75\%$ of this curved surface area:
$$\text{Value} = 0.75 \times 2772 = 2079 \approx 2080\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A hollow sphere has an outer radius of $4\text{ cm}$ and inner radius of $1\text{ cm}$. What is the volume of this hollow sphere?
questions.solution:
Volume of hollow sphere:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi (R^3 - r^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (4^3 - 1^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (64 - 1) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (63) = 84\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: What is the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of a spherical shell whose inner and outer radii are respectively $2\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Volume of spherical shell:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi (R^3 - r^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3^3 - 2^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (27 - 8) = \frac{76\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: If the diameter of a hemisphere is $21\text{ cm}$, then the curved surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the hemisphere is: $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 21\text{ cm} \implies r = \frac{21}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Curved surface area:
$$\text{CSA} = 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{21}{2}\right)^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{441}{4} = 693\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The dome of a residential tower is in the form of a hemisphere with radius of $560\text{ cm}$. Find the cost of painting it at the rate of ₹$25\text{ per }\text{m}^2$. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 560\text{ cm} = 5.6\text{ m}$.
Curved surface area:
$$\text{CSA} = 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times (5.6)^2 = \frac{44}{7} \times 31.36 = 197.12\text{ m}^2$$
Total cost at ₹$25/\text{m}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 197.12 \times 25 = ₹4928$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical dome of a building needs to be painted. If the circumference of the base of the dome is $154\text{ cm}$, then find the cost of painting it if the cost of painting is ₹$4\text{ per }100\text{ cm}^2$ $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Circumference $2\pi r = 154 \implies 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 154 \implies r = \frac{49}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Curved surface area:
$$\text{CSA} = 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{49}{2}\right)^2 = 3773\text{ cm}^2$$
Cost at ₹$4$ per $100\text{ cm}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 3773 \times \frac{4}{100} = ₹150.92$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl made of iron has inner diameter $84\text{ cm}$. Find the cost of tin plating it on the inside at the rate of ₹$21\text{ per }100\text{ cm}^2$ $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$ correct to two places of decimal.
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 84\text{ cm} \implies r = 42\text{ cm}$.
Inside curved surface area:
$$\text{CSA} = 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 42^2 = 11088\text{ cm}^2$$
Cost of tin plating at ₹$21$ per $100\text{ cm}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 11088 \times \frac{21}{100} = ₹2328.48$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A hemisphere has a radius of $6.2\text{ cm}$. Find its total surface area $(\text{use } \pi = 3.14)$ (round off two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Total surface area of hemisphere:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3 \times 3.14 \times (6.2)^2 = 9.42 \times 38.44 = 362.1048 \approx 362.10\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: Find the total surface area of a hemisphere with a radius of $11\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Total surface area of a hemisphere:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi (11^2) = 363\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of diameter $28\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 28\text{ cm} \implies r = 14\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 3 \times 22 \times 28 = 1848\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: Determine the total surface area of a hemisphere closed at bottom. Radius of the hemisphere is $\sqrt{\frac{25}{\pi}}\text{ unit}$.
questions.solution:
Total surface area of a closed hemisphere:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi \left(\sqrt{\frac{25}{\pi}}\right)^2 = 3\pi \times \frac{25}{\pi} = 75\text{ unit}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A solid sphere has a surface area of $616\text{ cm}^2$. This sphere is now cut into two hemispheres. What is the total surface area of one of the hemispheres?
questions.solution:
Surface area of sphere $= 4\pi r^2 = 616 \implies \pi r^2 = 154\text{ cm}^2$.
Total surface area of one hemisphere:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3 \times 154 = 462\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The diameter of a hemisphere is equal to the diagonal of a rectangle of length $4\text{ cm}$ and breadth $3\text{ cm}$. Find the total surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the hemisphere.
questions.solution:
Diagonal of rectangle $d = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5\text{ cm}$.
Diameter of hemisphere $= 5\text{ cm} \implies r = \frac{5}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{75\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl has $21\text{ cm}$ radius. It is to be painted inside as well as outside. The cost of painting it at the rate of ₹$0.05\text{ per }\text{cm}^2$ and assuming that the thickness of the bowl is negligible, is: $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Total painted area = inside CSA + outside CSA:
$$\text{Area} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r^2 = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 = 5544\text{ cm}^2$$
Cost at ₹$0.05$ per $\text{cm}^2$:
$$\text{Cost} = 5544 \times 0.05 = ₹277.20$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the radius of a hemispherical balloon increases from $4\text{ cm}$ to $7\text{ cm}$ as air is pumped into it, find the ratio of the surface area of the new balloon to its original.
questions.solution:
Ratio of surface areas:
$$\frac{S_{\text{new}}}{S_{\text{orig}}} = \left(\frac{r_{\text{new}}}{r_{\text{orig}}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{16} = 49 : 16$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The curved surface area of a solid hemisphere is $22\text{ cm}^2$. What is the total surface area of the hemisphere? $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Given $\text{CSA} = 2\pi r^2 = 22\text{ cm}^2 \implies \pi r^2 = 11\text{ cm}^2$.
Total surface area:
$$\text{TSA} = 3\pi r^2 = 3 \times 11 = 33\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A solid sphere of diameter $7\text{ cm}$ is cut into two equal halves. What will be the increase in its total surface area?
questions.solution:
When a sphere is cut into two hemispheres, two circular cross-sections of area $\pi r^2$ each are exposed.
Increase in total surface area:
$$\Delta A = 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2 = 77\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: What will be the difference between the total surface area and the curved surface area of a hemisphere having $4\text{ cm}$ diameter?
questions.solution:
Difference between total surface area and curved surface area:
$$\text{TSA} - \text{CSA} = 3\pi r^2 - 2\pi r^2 = \pi r^2$$
Given $d = 4\text{ cm} \implies r = 2\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Difference} = \pi (2^2) = 4\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The radius of a hemispherical bowl is $9\text{ cm}$. The capacity of the bowl is: $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Capacity of the bowl:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 9^3 = \frac{44 \times 243}{7} = \frac{10692}{7} \approx 1527.43\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: Find the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of a hemisphere of radius $18\text{ cm}$. $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$ (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
Volume of hemisphere:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 18^3 = \frac{44 \times 1944}{7} = \frac{85536}{7} \approx 12219.43\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: How many liters of water can a hemispherical tank of radius $2.1\text{m}$ contain? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Volume of the tank:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (2.1)^3 = \frac{44}{21} \times 9.261 = 19.404\text{ m}^3$$
Since $1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ liters}$:
$$\text{Capacity} = 19.404 \times 1000 = 19404\text{ liters}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The volume of the hemisphere (to the nearest integer) with a radius of $5.5\text{ cm}$ is: $(\text{use } \pi = 3.14)$
questions.solution:
Volume of hemisphere:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times 3.14 \times (5.5)^3 = \frac{6.28 \times 166.375}{3} \approx 348.28 \approx 348\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the diameter of a hemisphere is $42\text{ cm}$, then the volume of hemisphere (in $\text{cm}^3$) is: $\text{Take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 42\text{ cm} \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$.
Volume of hemisphere:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^3 = 44 \times 441 = 19404\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The diameter of a hemispherical bowl is $21\text{ cm}$. The volume of the bowl is equal to: $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Diameter $= 21\text{ cm} \implies r = 10.5\text{ cm} = \frac{21}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Volume of bowl:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{21}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{4851}{2} = 2425.5\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is $4158\text{ cm}^2$. Find its volume (in $\text{cm}^3$).
questions.solution:
Total surface area $= 3\pi r^2 = 4158$:
$$3 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 = 4158 \implies r^2 = 441 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$$
Volume of the hemisphere:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^3 = 44 \times 441 = 19404\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl whose radius is $21\text{ cm}$ is full of ice cream. Find the volume of the ice cream. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Radius $r = 21\text{ cm}$.
Volume of the hemispherical bowl:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^3 = 44 \times 441 = 19404\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A sphere and another solid hemisphere have the same surface area. The ratio of their volumes is:
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the sphere be $r_1$ and the radius of the solid hemisphere be $r_2$.
Given surface area of sphere = total surface area of solid hemisphere:
$$4\pi r_1^2 = 3\pi r_2^2 \implies \frac{r_1^2}{r_2^2} = \frac{3}{4} \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$
Ratio of their volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\pi r_1^3}{\frac{2}{3}\pi r_2^3} = 2 \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3 = 2 \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^3 = 2 \times \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{8} = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4} = 3\sqrt{3} : 4$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl is $88\text{ cm}$ round the brim. Assuming it to be full, how many persons may be served from it in hemispherical glasses, $7\text{ cm}$ in diameter at the top? $(\text{Where } \pi = 22/7)$
questions.solution:
Circumference of the brim of the bowl $2\pi R = 88\text{ cm}$:
$$2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times R = 88 \implies R = 14\text{ cm}$$
Radius of hemispherical glass $r = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5\text{ cm}$.
Number of persons served:
$$n = \frac{\text{Volume of bowl}}{\text{Volume of one glass}} = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{14}{3.5}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: If the radius of a sphere is thrice than the radius of the hemisphere, then what will be the respective ratio of their volumes?
questions.solution:
Let radius of hemisphere be $r$, so radius of sphere $R = 3r$.
Ratio of their volumes:
$$\frac{V_{\text{sphere}}}{V_{\text{hemisphere}}} = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3}{\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3} = 2 \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = 2 \times (3)^3 = 2 \times 27 = 54 = 54 : 1$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The internal diameter of a hollow hemispherical vessel is $24\text{ cm}$. It is made of a steel sheet which is $0.5\text{ cm}$ thick. What is the total surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the vessel?
questions.solution:
Internal radius $r = \frac{24}{2} = 12\text{ cm}$.
External radius $R = 12 + 0.5 = 12.5\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area of hollow hemispherical vessel:
$$\text{TSA} = 2\pi R^2 + 2\pi r^2 + \pi (R^2 - r^2) = \pi (3R^2 + r^2)$$
$$\text{TSA} = \pi [3(12.5)^2 + 12^2] = \pi [3(156.25) + 144] = \pi [468.75 + 144] = 612.75\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The inner and outer radii of a hemispherical wooden bowl are $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$, respectively. Its entire surface has to be polished and the cost of polishing $\pi\text{ cm}^2$ is $\text{Rs.}50$. How much will it cost to polish the bowl?
questions.solution:
Inner radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$, outer radius $R = 8\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area:
$$\text{TSA} = \pi (3R^2 + r^2) = \pi [3(8^2) + 6^2] = \pi [192 + 36] = 228\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Cost of polishing $\pi\text{ cm}^2$ is Rs. 50:
$$\text{Total Cost} = \frac{228\pi}{\pi} \times 50 = 228 \times 50 = \text{Rs. } 11400$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The internal and external radii of a hollow hemispherical vessel are $6\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$ respectively. What is the total surface are (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the vessel?
questions.solution:
Internal radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$, external radius $R = 7\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area of hollow hemisphere:
$$\text{TSA} = \pi (3R^2 + r^2) = \pi [3(7^2) + 6^2] = \pi [147 + 36] = 183\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl is made of $1\text{ cm}$ thick steel. The inside radius of the bowl is $4\text{cm}$. The volume of the steel (in $\text{cm}^3$) used in making the bowl is:
questions.solution:
Inside radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$, thickness $= 1\text{ cm} \implies$ outside radius $R = 4 + 1 = 5\text{ cm}$.
Volume of steel:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi (R^3 - r^3) = \frac{2}{3}\pi (5^3 - 4^3) = \frac{2}{3}\pi (125 - 64) = \frac{2}{3}\pi (61) = \frac{122}{3}\pi = 40\frac{2}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: If the inner radius of a hemispherical bowl is $5\text{ cm}$ and its thickness is $0.25\text{ cm}$, then find the volume of the material required in making the bowl, $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$ (Rounded up to two places of decimals)
questions.solution:
Inner radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$, outer radius $R = 5 + 0.25 = 5.25 = \frac{21}{4}\text{ cm}$.
Volume of material:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi (R^3 - r^3) = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left[\left(\frac{21}{4}\right)^3 - 5^3\right] = \frac{44}{21} \times [144.703125 - 125] = \frac{44}{21} \times 19.703125 \approx 41.28\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl is made of silver and has an inner diameter of $4\text{ cm}$ if the thickness of silver is $0.5\text{ cm}$. Find the volume of silver used in making the bowl correct to two places of decimals $(\text{use } \pi = 3.14)$.
questions.solution:
Inner diameter $= 4\text{ cm} \implies r = 2\text{ cm}$.
Outer radius $R = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5\text{ cm}$.
Volume of silver:
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi (R^3 - r^3) = \frac{2}{3} \times 3.14 \times (2.5^3 - 2^3) = \frac{6.28}{3} \times (15.625 - 8) = \frac{6.28 \times 7.625}{3} \approx 15.96\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: If a cuboid of dimensions $32\text{ cm} \times 12\text{cm} \times 9\text{cm}$ is melted into two cubes of same size, what will be the ratio of the surface area of the cuboid to the total surface area of the two cubes?
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $= 32 \times 12 \times 9 = 3456\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of each cube $= \frac{3456}{2} = 1728\text{ cm}^3 \implies a = \sqrt[3]{1728} = 12\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of cuboid $= 2(32 \times 12 + 12 \times 9 + 32 \times 9) = 2(384 + 108 + 288) = 1560\text{ cm}^2$.
Total surface area of two cubes $= 2 \times 6a^2 = 12 \times 12^2 = 1728\text{ cm}^2$.
Ratio:
$$\frac{\text{Surface Area of Cuboid}}{\text{Total Surface Area of Two Cubes}} = \frac{1560}{1728} = \frac{65}{72}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A large solid cube is melted and cast into 'N' small solid spheres, each of radius $3\text{ cm}$, and 'N + 2' small solid cuboids, each of dimensions $4\text{ cm} \times 4\text{ cm} \times 6.5\text{ cm}$. If the length of each side of the large solid cube is $12\text{ cm}$, then find the value of 'N'. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Volume of large cube $= 12^3 = 1728\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of one sphere $= \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3^3 = \frac{792}{7}\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of one cuboid $= 4 \times 4 \times 6.5 = 104\text{ cm}^3$.
Total volume equation:
$$N \times \frac{792}{7} + (N + 2) \times 104 = 1728$$
$$\frac{792N}{7} + 104N + 208 = 1728$$
$$N \left(\frac{792 + 728}{7}\right) = 1520 \implies \frac{1520N}{7} = 1520 \implies N = 7$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A cylindrical metallic rod of diameter $2\text{ cm}$ and length $45\text{ cm}$ is melted and converted into wire of uniform thickness and length $5\text{ m}$. The diameter of the wire is:
questions.solution:
Cylinder rod: radius $R = 1\text{ cm}$, length $H = 45\text{ cm}$.
Wire: length $h = 5\text{ m} = 500\text{ cm}$, radius $= r$.
Volume is conserved:
$$\pi R^2 H = \pi r^2 h \implies 1^2 \times 45 = r^2 \times 500 \implies r^2 = \frac{45}{500} = \frac{9}{100} \implies r = \frac{3}{10}\text{ cm} = 3\text{ mm}$$
Diameter of the wire $= 2r = 6\text{ mm}$.
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: The ratio of the diameters of two spheres is given as $1 : 4$. The larger sphere is melted and 125 identical spheres are made out of the molten material. The smaller sphere is melted and 27 identical spheres are made out of the molten material. If the ratio of the volume of each of the 125 identical spheres to the volume of each of the 27 identical spheres is given as $1 : m$, what is the value of m?
questions.solution:
Let the diameters of smaller and larger spheres be $d$ and $4d$, so their volumes are $V$ and $64V$.
Volume of each of 125 small spheres $= \frac{64V}{125}$.
Volume of each of 27 small spheres $= \frac{V}{27}$.
Ratio of volume of each of the 125 spheres to that of the 27 spheres:
$$\frac{64V / 125}{V / 27} = \frac{64 \times 27}{125} = \frac{1728}{125}$$
Given this ratio is $1 : m = \frac{1}{m}$:
$$\frac{1}{m} = \frac{1728}{125} \implies m = \frac{125}{1728}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: The radii of the ends of a frustum of a solid right-circular cone $45\text{ cm}$ high are $28\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$. If this frustum is melted and reconstructed into a solid right circular cylinder whose radius of base and height are in the ratio 3: 5, find the curved surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of this cylinder. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Volume of frustum:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi h (R^2 + r^2 + Rr) = \frac{1}{3}\pi (45) [28^2 + 7^2 + 28 \times 7] = 15\pi [784 + 49 + 196] = 15435\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Let radius and height of cylinder be $3x$ and $5x$.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi (3x)^2 (5x) = 45\pi x^3$.
$$45\pi x^3 = 15435\pi \implies x^3 = 343 \implies x = 7$$
Radius $r_c = 3(7) = 21\text{ cm}$, height $h_c = 5(7) = 35\text{ cm}$.
Curved surface area of cylinder:
$$\text{CSA} = 2\pi r_c h_c = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 35 = 4620\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A frustum of a right circular cone whose height is $18\text{ cm}$, large base radius is $25\text{ cm}$ and small base radius is $20\text{ cm}$, is melted to form a small sphere of diameter $2\text{ cm}$. How many spheres will be formed?
questions.solution:
Volume of frustum:
$$V_f = \frac{1}{3}\pi h (R^2 + r^2 + Rr) = \frac{1}{3}\pi (18) [25^2 + 20^2 + 25 \times 20] = 6\pi [625 + 400 + 500] = 9150\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Diameter of sphere $= 2\text{ cm} \implies$ radius $= 1\text{ cm}$.
Volume of sphere $V_s = \frac{4}{3}\pi (1^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of spheres:
$$n = \frac{9150\pi}{\frac{4}{3}\pi} = \frac{9150 \times 3}{4} = 6862.5 \approx 6862$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: 3 solid spheres of diameters $6\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ are melted together to form a single solid sphere. Find its radius.
questions.solution:
Radii of three spheres are $r_1 = 3\text{ cm}$, $r_2 = 4\text{ cm}$, $r_3 = 5\text{ cm}$.
Let the radius of new sphere be $R$:
$$R^3 = r_1^3 + r_2^3 + r_3^3 = 3^3 + 4^3 + 5^3 = 27 + 64 + 125 = 216 = 6^3 \implies R = 6\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid copper sphere of radius $9\text{ cm}$ is drawn in to a wire of radius $4\text{mm}$. Find the length of the wire.
questions.solution:
Radius of sphere $R = 9\text{ cm}$. Radius of wire $r = 4\text{ mm} = 0.4\text{ cm}$.
Volume of sphere = Volume of wire:
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \pi r^2 L$$
$$\frac{4}{3} \times 9^3 = (0.4)^2 \times L$$
$$972 = 0.16 L \implies L = \frac{972}{0.16} = 6075\text{ cm} = 60.75\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: If three spheres of radius $75\text{cm}$, $60\text{ cm}$ and $45\text{ cm}$ are melted into one big sphere, then the radius of the big sphere is;
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the big sphere be $R$:
$$R^3 = 75^3 + 60^3 + 45^3 = 15^3 (5^3 + 4^3 + 3^3) = 15^3 (125 + 64 + 27) = 15^3 \times 216 = 15^3 \times 6^3 = (90)^3$$
$$R = 90\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid metallic cube having surface area of $54\text{ cm}^2$ is melted to form smaller cubes of surface area $\frac{8}{12}\text{ cm}^2$ each. Find the number of smaller cubes.
questions.solution:
For the original cube: $6A^2 = 54 \implies A^2 = 9 \implies A = 3\text{ cm}$.
For each small cube: $6a^2 = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3} \implies a^2 = \frac{1}{9} \implies a = \frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}$.
Number of small cubes:
$$n = \left(\frac{A}{a}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{3}{1/3}\right)^3 = 9^3 = 729$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A metallic sphere of volume $3136\pi\text{ cm}^3$ is melted and then, recast into smaller, cones each of radius $3.5\text{ cm}$ and height $4\text{ cm}$. How many cones are obtained?
questions.solution:
Volume of each small cone:
$$V_c = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (3.5^2)(4) = \frac{1}{3}\pi (12.25)(4) = \frac{49}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Number of cones obtained:
$$n = \frac{3136\pi}{\frac{49}{3}\pi} = \frac{3136 \times 3}{49} = 64 \times 3 = 192$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A cylinderical rod of iron whose height is twelve items its radius, is melted and cast into spherical balls, each of one-third the radius of the cylinder. Find the number of spherical balls.
questions.solution:
Let radius of cylinder be $r$, then height $h = 12r$.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r^2 (12r) = 12\pi r^3$.
Radius of each spherical ball $= \frac{r}{3}$.
Volume of each spherical ball $= \frac{4}{3}\pi \left(\frac{r}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{4\pi r^3}{81}$.
Number of spherical balls:
$$n = \frac{12\pi r^3}{\frac{4\pi r^3}{81}} = 12 \times \frac{81}{4} = 3 \times 81 = 243$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: Three solid cubes of metal have sides $6\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$, respectively. They are melted to form a new cube. What is the surface area of this new cube?
questions.solution:
Volume of new cube:
$$V = 6^3 + 8^3 + 10^3 = 216 + 512 + 1000 = 1728\text{ cm}^3$$
Edge of new cube $a = \sqrt[3]{1728} = 12\text{ cm}$.
Surface area of new cube:
$$\text{SA} = 6a^2 = 6 \times 12^2 = 6 \times 144 = 864\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid metallic cylinder of base radius $6\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$ is melted to form small cylinders, each of height $2.5\text{ cm}$ and base radius $2\text{ cm}$. Find the number of small cylinders.
questions.solution:
Number of small cylinders:
$$n = \frac{\pi R^2 H}{\pi r^2 h} = \frac{6^2 \times 10}{2^2 \times 2.5} = \frac{36 \times 10}{4 \times 2.5} = \frac{360}{10} = 36$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A cylindrical candle, $14\text{ cm}$ in diameter and length $2\text{ cm}$ is melted to form a cuboid candle of dimensions $7\text{ cm} \times 11\text{ cm} \times 2\text{ cm}$. How many cuboidal candles can be obtained?
questions.solution:
Radius of cylindrical candle $r = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$, height $h = 2\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cylinder $= \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times 2 = 308\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of one cuboid candle $= 7 \times 11 \times 2 = 154\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of cuboidal candles:
$$n = \frac{308}{154} = 2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid metallic sphere of radius $6\text{ cm}$ is melted and recast into spherical balls of radius $3\text{ cm}$. The number of spherical balls thus obtained is:
questions.solution:
Number of balls:
$$n = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{6}{3}\right)^3 = 2^3 = 8$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid sphere of radius $8\text{ cm}$ is melted and then recast into small spherical balls each of diameter $4\text{ cm}$. Find the number of balls thus obtained $\left(\text{used } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$.
questions.solution:
Radius of large sphere $R = 8\text{ cm}$. Radius of small ball $r = \frac{4}{2} = 2\text{ cm}$.
Number of balls:
$$n = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{8}{2}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A metallic solid cuboid of dimensions $36\text{ cm} \times 22\text{ cm} \times 12\text{ cm}$ is melted and recast in the form of cubes of side $6\text{cm}$. Find the number of the cubes so formed.
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $= 36 \times 22 \times 12\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of each cube $= 6^3 = 216\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of cubes formed:
$$n = \frac{36 \times 22 \times 12}{216} = \frac{432 \times 22}{216} = 2 \times 22 = 44$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A copper sphere of diameter $12\text{ cm}$ is drawn into a wire of diameter $4\text{ mm}$. What is the length (in cm) of the wire? $(\text{Use } \pi = 22/7)$
questions.solution:
Sphere radius $R = 6\text{ cm}$. Wire radius $r = \frac{4}{2}\text{ mm} = 2\text{ mm} = 0.2\text{ cm}$.
Volume of sphere = Volume of wire:
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \pi r^2 L$$
$$\frac{4}{3} \times 6^3 = (0.2)^2 \times L$$
$$288 = 0.04 L \implies L = \frac{288}{0.04} = 7200\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A hollow sphere of external and internal diameters of $10\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}$, respectively, is melted and made into another solid in the shape of a right circular cone of base diameter $10\text{ cm}$. Find the height of the cone.
questions.solution:
Hollow sphere: external radius $R = 5\text{ cm}$, internal radius $r = 3\text{ cm}$.
Volume of hollow sphere:
$$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi (5^3 - 3^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (125 - 27) = \frac{392}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Cone: base radius $r_c = 5\text{ cm}$, height $= h$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi (5^2) h = \frac{25}{3}\pi h$.
$$\frac{25}{3}\pi h = \frac{392}{3}\pi \implies 25h = 392 \implies h = \frac{392}{25} = 15.68\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid metal cylinder of $12\text{ cm}$ height and $7\text{ cm}$ radius is melted and recast into two cones in the proportion of $1 : 2$ (volume), keeping the height $12\text{ cm}$. What would be the percentage change in the flat surface area before and after $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Initial flat surface area of cylinder (two circular bases):
$$A_1 = 2\pi R^2 = 2\pi (7^2) = 98\pi$$
Volume of cylinder $= \pi R^2 H = \pi (49)(12) = 588\pi$.
Volumes of two cones in ratio $1 : 2$:
$$V_1 = \frac{1}{3}(588\pi) = 196\pi, \quad V_2 = \frac{2}{3}(588\pi) = 392\pi$$
Each cone has height $h = 12\text{ cm}$:
$$\frac{1}{3}\pi r_1^2 (12) = 196\pi \implies r_1^2 = 49$$
$$\frac{1}{3}\pi r_2^2 (12) = 392\pi \implies r_2^2 = 98$$
Flat surface area of both cones (their bases):
$$A_2 = \pi r_1^2 + \pi r_2^2 = 49\pi + 98\pi = 147\pi$$
Percentage change in flat surface area:
$$\frac{A_2 - A_1}{A_1} \times 100\% = \frac{147\pi - 98\pi}{98\pi} \times 100\% = \frac{49}{98} \times 100\% = 50\%$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: Melting a metal ball of radius 3 units, 27 identical dice and a ball of radius 1 units are made. What is the side of dice?
questions.solution:
Volume of large ball $V_1 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3^3) = 36\pi$.
Volume of small ball $V_2 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (1^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi$.
Volume of 27 dice:
$$27 a^3 = 36\pi - \frac{4}{3}\pi = \frac{104}{3}\pi \approx \frac{104 \times 3.1416}{3} \approx 108.905$$
$$a^3 = \frac{108.905}{27} \approx 4.0335 \implies a \approx 1.592 \approx 1.6\text{ units}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid cube, whose each edge is of length $48\text{ cm}$, is melted. Identical solid cubes, each of volume $64\text{ cm}^3$, are made out of this molten cube, without any wastage. How many such small cubes are obtained?
questions.solution:
Volume of large cube $= 48^3 = 110592\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of small cubes:
$$n = \frac{110592}{64} = 1728$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid sphere made of wax of radius $12\text{ cm}$ is melted and cast into solid hemispheres of radius $4\text{ cm}$ each. Find the number of such solid hemispheres.
questions.solution:
Number of hemispheres:
$$n = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3}{\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3} = 2 \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = 2 \left(\frac{12}{4}\right)^3 = 2 \times 3^3 = 2 \times 27 = 54$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: The radius of a metallic spherical ball is $3\text{ cm}$. If the metallic ball is melted and recast into $x$ number of hemispheres of radius equal to half the radius of the metallic spherical ball, then find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
Radius of hemisphere $r = \frac{R}{2}$.
$$x = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3}{\frac{2}{3}\pi (R/2)^3} = 2 \times 2^3 = 16$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: The diameter of a metallic sphere is $6\text{ cm}$. It is melted and drawn into a wire having a diameter of the cross section as $0.4\text{ cm}$. Find the length of the wire (in meters).
questions.solution:
Radius of sphere $R = 3\text{ cm}$. Radius of wire $r = 0.2\text{ cm}$.
Volume of sphere = Volume of wire:
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \pi r^2 L$$
$$\frac{4}{3} \times 27 = (0.2)^2 L \implies 36 = 0.04 L \implies L = 900\text{ cm} = 9\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A cuboid with dimension $2 \times 4 \times 1\text{ units}$ is melted and a new cube is made. What is the total surface area of the cube formed in square units?
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $= 2 \times 4 \times 1 = 8\text{ units}^3$.
Side of the cube $a = \sqrt[3]{8} = 2\text{ units}$.
Total surface area of the cube:
$$\text{TSA} = 6a^2 = 6(2^2) = 24\text{ square units}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: Two cuboids of dimension $2 \times 3 \times 4\text{ units}$ and $2 \times 5 \times 4\text{ units}$ are melted and a single cube is made. What is the side of the cube in units?
questions.solution:
Total volume $= (2 \times 3 \times 4) + (2 \times 5 \times 4) = 24 + 40 = 64\text{ units}^3$.
Side of the cube:
$$a = \sqrt[3]{64} = 4.0\text{ units}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid metallic cuboid of length $11\text{ cm}$, breadth $8\text{ cm}$ and height $6\text{ cm}$ is melted and reshaped to form a cone of height $14\text{ cm}$. What is the radius of the cone thus formed?
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $= 11 \times 8 \times 6 = 528\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of cone:
$$\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = 528$$
$$\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 \times 14 = 528$$
$$\frac{44}{3} r^2 = 528 \implies r^2 = \frac{528 \times 3}{44} = 36 \implies r = 6\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: The sides of three cubes of metal are $15\text{ cm}$, $18\text{ cm}$ and $25\text{ cm}$, respectively. Find the side (in cm) of the new cube formed by melting these cubes together
questions.solution:
Total volume of the three cubes:
$$V = 15^3 + 18^3 + 25^3 = 3375 + 5832 + 15625 = 24832\text{ cm}^3$$
Side of the new cube:
$$a = \sqrt[3]{24832} = \sqrt[3]{64 \times 388} = 4\sqrt[3]{388}\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid rectangular block of metal of dimensions $88\text{ cm} \times 21\text{ cm} \times 21\text{ cm}$, is melted to form a solid sphere. What is its radius (in cm)? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Volume of block = Volume of sphere:
$$88 \times 21 \times 21 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^3$$
$$88 \times 441 = \frac{88}{21} r^3 \implies r^3 = 441 \times 21 = 21^3 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: How many solid spheres are made if a metallic cone of radius $12\text{ cm}$ and height $24\text{ cm}$ is melted into sphere of radius $2\text{ cm}$ each?
questions.solution:
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi (12^2)(24) = 1152\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of one sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi (2^3) = \frac{32}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of spheres:
$$n = \frac{1152\pi}{\frac{32}{3}\pi} = \frac{1152 \times 3}{32} = 36 \times 3 = 108$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid cuboid is melted to form a number of cubes. If the length, breadth and height of cuboid are $20\text{ cm}$, $16\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ and the edge of each cube is $4\text{ cm}$, then the number of cubes is:
questions.solution:
Number of cubes:
$$n = \frac{20 \times 16 \times 8}{4 \times 4 \times 4} = 5 \times 4 \times 2 = 40$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A metallic sphere of radius $21\text{ cm}$ is melted and then recast into smaller cones each with a radius of $7\text{ cm}$, and a height of $3\text{ cm}$. Find the number of cones obtained.
questions.solution:
Volume of sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi (21^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (9261) = 12348\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of each cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi (7^2)(3) = 49\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of cones:
$$n = \frac{12348\pi}{49\pi} = 252$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A solid sphere of radius $4\text{ cm}$ is melted and cast into the shape of a solid cone of height $4\text{ cm}$. The radius of the base of the cone is
questions.solution:
Volume of sphere = Volume of cone:
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi (4^3) = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 (4)$$
$$4 \times 64 = 4r^2 \implies r^2 = 64 \implies r = 8\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: A spherical ball of lead, $3\text{ cm}$ in diameter is melted and recast into three spherical balls. The diameters of two of these balls are $\frac{3}{2}\text{ cm}$ and $2\text{ cm}$, respectively. Find the diameter of the third ball.
questions.solution:
Let the diameter of the third ball be $d_3$.
Volume conservation for spheres gives:
$$D^3 = d_1^3 + d_2^3 + d_3^3$$
$$3^3 = (1.5)^3 + 2^3 + d_3^3$$
$$27 = 3.375 + 8 + d_3^3 = 11.375 + d_3^3$$
$$d_3^3 = 27 - 11.375 = 15.625 = (2.5)^3 \implies d_3 = 2.5\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: CONCEPT OF MELTING & RECASTING
questions.questionText: Three cubes with sides in the ratio of $3 : 4 : 5$ are melted to form a single cube whose diagonal is $18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. The sides of the three cubes are:
questions.solution:
Diagonal of new cube $= a\sqrt{3} = 18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm} \implies a = 18\text{ cm}$.
Volume of new cube $= 18^3 = 5832\text{ cm}^3$.
Let the sides of three cubes be $3x, 4x, 5x$:
$$(3x)^3 + (4x)^3 + (5x)^3 = 5832$$
$$(27 + 64 + 125)x^3 = 5832 \implies 216x^3 = 5832 \implies x^3 = 27 \implies x = 3$$
Sides of the three cubes are:
$$3(3) = 9\text{ cm}, \quad 4(3) = 12\text{ cm}, \quad 5(3) = 15\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: The internal and external diameters of a hollow hemispherical bowl are $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$, respectively. If it is melted and recast into a solid cylinder of diameter $14\text{ cm}$, what is the height of the cylinder in $\text{cm}$?
questions.solution:
Internal radius $r = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ cm}$, external radius $R = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ cm}$.
Volume of hollow hemisphere $= \frac{2}{3}\pi (R^3 - r^3) = \frac{2}{3}\pi (5^3 - 3^3) = \frac{2}{3}\pi (125 - 27) = \frac{2}{3}\pi (98) = \frac{196}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
For the solid cylinder, radius $r_c = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r_c^2 h = \pi (7)^2 h = 49\pi h$.
Equating volumes:
$$49\pi h = \frac{196}{3}\pi \implies h = \frac{196}{3 \times 49} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: Melting a hemisphere of radius $7\text{ cm}$, four small identical spheres are made. What is the radius of these spheres?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of each small sphere be $r$.
Volume of hemisphere $= \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (7)^3$.
Volume of $4$ identical spheres $= 4 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{16}{3}\pi r^3$.
Equating volumes:
$$\frac{16}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (343) \implies 16r^3 = 686 \implies r^3 = \frac{343}{8}$$
$$r = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A solid iron sphere of radius $21\text{ cm}$ is melted down into a cone of height $84\text{ cm}$. What will be the radius of the cone?
questions.solution:
Volume of sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (21)^3$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 (84)$.
Equating volumes:
$$\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 (84) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (21)^3$$
$$84 r^2 = 4 \times 21 \times 21^2 = 84 \times 21^2 \implies r^2 = 21^2 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: How many solid spherical balls of radius $6\text{ cm}$ can be made by melting a solid hemisphere of radius $12\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Number of balls $n = \frac{\text{Volume of hemisphere}}{\text{Volume of one sphere}} = \frac{\frac{2}{3}\pi R^3}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3} = \frac{R^3}{2r^3}$.
$$n = \frac{12^3}{2 \times 6^3} = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(\frac{12}{6}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2^3 = 4$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: $24$ equal solid hemispheres are melted to form a right circular cylinder of radius $12\text{ cm}$ and height $24\text{ cm}$. Find the radius of each solid hemisphere.
questions.solution:
Volume of $24$ hemispheres $= 24 \times \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = 16\pi r^3$.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi R^2 H = \pi (12)^2 (24) = 3456\pi$.
Equating volumes:
$$16\pi r^3 = 3456\pi \implies r^3 = \frac{3456}{16} = 216 \implies r = 6\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: Three metallic cubes whose sides are $6\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ respectively are melted and converted into a single cube. If there is no loss of metal in this process, then what is the length of the side of the new cube?
questions.solution:
Volume of the new cube $A^3 = a_1^3 + a_2^3 + a_3^3$.
$$A^3 = 6^3 + 8^3 + 10^3 = 216 + 512 + 1000 = 1728\text{ cm}^3$$
$$A = \sqrt[3]{1728} = 12\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: How many spherical lead shots each of diameter $8.4\text{ cm}$ can be obtained from a rectangular solid of lead with dimension $88\text{ cm}, 63\text{ cm}, 42\text{ cm}$ $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Radius of spherical lead shot $r = \frac{8.4}{2} = 4.2\text{ cm}$.
Volume of rectangular solid $= 88 \times 63 \times 42\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of one spherical shot $= \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (4.2)^3$.
Number of lead shots:
$$n = \frac{88 \times 63 \times 42}{\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 4.2 \times 4.2 \times 4.2} = \frac{88 \times 63 \times 42}{\frac{88}{21} \times 74.088} = \frac{232848}{310.464} = 750$$
Hence, the correct option is B.
