questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A copper sphere of diameter $18\text{ cm}$ is drawn into a wire of diameter $6\text{ mm}$. Find the length of the wire.
questions.solution:
Radius of sphere $R = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ cm}$.
Radius of wire $r = \frac{6}{2}\text{ mm} = 3\text{ mm} = 0.3\text{ cm}$.
Volume of sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (9)^3 = 972\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of wire $= \pi r^2 L = \pi (0.3)^2 L = 0.09\pi L$.
Equating volumes:
$$0.09\pi L = 972\pi \implies L = \frac{972}{0.09} = 10800\text{ cm} = 108\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A cuboid of length $36\text{ m}$, breadth $18\text{ m}$ and height $9\text{ m}$ is melted and recast into a cube. Find the length of the diagonal of the cube.
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $= l \times b \times h = 36 \times 18 \times 9 = 5832\text{ m}^3$.
Side of cube $a = \sqrt[3]{5832} = 18\text{ m}$.
Diagonal of cube $= a\sqrt{3} = 18\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A solid hemisphere has radius $21\text{ cm}$. It is melted to form a cylinder such that the ratio of its curved surface area to total surface area is $2 : 5$. What is the radius (in $\text{cm}$) of its base $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$?
questions.solution:
For the cylinder:
$$\frac{\text{CSA}}{\text{TSA}} = \frac{2\pi r h}{2\pi r(r + h)} = \frac{h}{r + h} = \frac{2}{5} \implies 5h = 2r + 2h \implies 3h = 2r \implies h = \frac{2}{3}r$$
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r^2 h = \pi r^2 \left(\frac{2}{3}r\right) = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3$.
Volume of hemisphere $= \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (21)^3$.
Equating volumes:
$$\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (21)^3 \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: An iron rod with diameter $4\text{ cm}$ and length $12\text{ cm}$ is drawn into a wire of length $12\text{ m}$ of uniform thickness. Determine the thickness of the wire.
questions.solution:
Radius of rod $R = \frac{4}{2} = 2\text{ cm}$, length $H = 12\text{ cm}$.
Volume of rod $= \pi R^2 H = \pi (2)^2 (12) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Length of wire $L = 12\text{ m} = 1200\text{ cm}$.
Let the radius of wire be $r$.
Volume of wire $= \pi r^2 L = 1200\pi r^2$.
Equating volumes:
$$1200\pi r^2 = 48\pi \implies r^2 = \frac{48}{1200} = \frac{4}{100} = 0.04 \implies r = 0.2\text{ cm}$$
Thickness (diameter) of wire $= 2r = 2 \times 0.2 = 0.4\text{ cm}$.
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A cuboid of sides $12\text{ cm}, 18\text{ cm}$ and $27\text{ cm}$ is melted to form a cube. What is the ratio of the total surface area of the cuboid to that of the cube?
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $= 12 \times 18 \times 27 = 5832\text{ cm}^3$.
Side of cube $a = \sqrt[3]{5832} = 18\text{ cm}$.
TSA of cuboid $= 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(12 \times 18 + 18 \times 27 + 27 \times 12) = 2(216 + 486 + 324) = 2(1026) = 2052\text{ cm}^2$.
TSA of cube $= 6a^2 = 6 \times 18^2 = 6 \times 324 = 1944\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{2052}{1944} = \frac{19}{18} = 19 : 18$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: The number of solid spheres, each of diameter $6\text{ cm}$, that could be moulded to form a solid metal cylinder of height $90\text{ cm}$ and diameter $4\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.solution:
Radius of sphere $r = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ cm}$.
Volume of one sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi (3)^3 = 36\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Radius of cylinder $R = \frac{4}{2} = 2\text{ cm}$, height $H = 90\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi R^2 H = \pi (2)^2 (90) = 360\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of spheres $n = \frac{360\pi}{36\pi} = 10$.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: The total surface area of a solid metallic hemisphere is $462\text{ cm}^2$. This is melted and moulded into a right circular cone. If the radius of the base of the cone is the same as that of the hemisphere, then its height is: $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
TSA of hemisphere $= 3\pi r^2 = 462\text{ cm}^2$.
$$3 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r^2 = 462 \implies r^2 = \frac{462 \times 7}{66} = 49 \implies r = 7\text{ cm}$$
Volume of hemisphere $= \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.
Equating volumes:
$$\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 \implies h = 2r = 2 \times 7 = 14\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: Radius of a large solid sphere is $14\text{ cm}$. It is melted to form $8$ equal small solid sphere. What is the sum of total surface areas of all the $8$ small solid spheres?
questions.solution:
Volume of large sphere $= 8 \times \text{Volume of small sphere}$.
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 8 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \implies R^3 = 8r^3 \implies r = \frac{R}{2} = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$$
Sum of TSA of $8$ small spheres $= 8 \times (4\pi r^2) = 32\pi r^2$.
$$= 32 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 = 32 \times 22 \times 7 = 4928\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: The radius of a solid sphere is $42\text{ cm}$. It is melted to form identical small solid spheres whose radius is $7\text{ cm}$. What is the number of small solid spheres obtained?
questions.solution:
Number of small solid spheres:
$$n = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{42}{7}\right)^3 = 6^3 = 216$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A metallic solid cuboid of dimensions $36\text{ cm} \times 18\text{ cm} \times 12\text{ cm}$ is melted and recast in the form of cubes of side $6\text{ cm}$. Find the number of cubes so formed.
questions.solution:
Number of cubes:
$$n = \frac{\text{Volume of cuboid}}{\text{Volume of one cube}} = \frac{36 \times 18 \times 12}{6 \times 6 \times 6} = 6 \times 3 \times 2 = 36$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: $15$ identical solid spherical balls of radius $5\text{ cm}$ are melted to form a single sphere. In this process, $35\%$ of the mass is wasted. What is the radius (in $\text{cm}$) of the single sphere that is now formed? [Give your answer correct to two decimal places.] $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Effective volume utilized $= (100 - 35)\% = 65\% = 0.65$.
Volume of $15$ balls $= 15 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi (5)^3$.
Volume of the single new sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$.
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 0.65 \times 15 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi (5)^3$$
$$R^3 = 0.65 \times 15 \times 125 = 9.75 \times 125 = 1218.75$$
$$R = \sqrt[3]{1218.75} \approx 10.68\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: How many small solid spheres each of $5\text{ mm}$ radius can be made out of a metallic solid cone whose base has radius $21\text{ cm}$ and height $30\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Radius of cone $R = 21\text{ cm}$, height $H = 30\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi R^2 H = \frac{1}{3}\pi (21)^2 (30) = 4410\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Radius of small sphere $r = 5\text{ mm} = 0.5\text{ cm} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Volume of one sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of spheres:
$$n = \frac{4410\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}} = 4410 \times 6 = 26460$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A solid cone of radius $7\text{ cm}$ and height $7\text{ cm}$ was melted along with two solid spheres of radius $7\text{ cm}$ each to form a solid cylinder of radius $7\text{ cm}$. What is the curved surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the cylinder? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
All solids share radius $r = 7\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi (7)^2 (7) = \frac{1}{3}\pi (7)^3$.
Volume of $2$ spheres $= 2 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi (7)^3 = \frac{8}{3}\pi (7)^3$.
Total melted volume $= \left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{8}{3}\right)\pi (7)^3 = 3\pi (7)^3$.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r^2 H = \pi (7)^2 H$.
Equating volumes:
$$\pi (7)^2 H = 3\pi (7)^3 \implies H = 3 \times 7 = 21\text{ cm}$$
Curved surface area of the cylinder $= 2\pi r H = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 21 = 44 \times 21 = 924\text{ cm}^2$.
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: The area of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal solid block of wax are $216\text{ cm}^2$, $96\text{ cm}^2$ and $144\text{ cm}^2$. It is melted and $8$ cubes of the same size are formed from it. What is the lateral surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of $3$ such cubes?
questions.solution:
Volume of cuboid $V = \sqrt{A_1 A_2 A_3} = \sqrt{216 \times 96 \times 144} = \sqrt{2985984} = 1728\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of each of the $8$ cubes $= \frac{1728}{8} = 216\text{ cm}^3$.
Side of each cube $a = \sqrt[3]{216} = 6\text{ cm}$.
Lateral surface area of $1$ cube $= 4a^2 = 4 \times 6^2 = 144\text{ cm}^2$.
Lateral surface area of $3$ such cubes $= 3 \times 144 = 432\text{ cm}^2$.
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A solid metallic cube of side $9\text{ cm}$ and a solid metallic cuboid having dimensions $5\text{ cm}, 13\text{ cm}, 31\text{ cm}$ melted and recast into a single cube. What is the total surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the new cube?
questions.solution:
Volume of cube $= 9^3 = 729\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of cuboid $= 5 \times 13 \times 31 = 2015\text{ cm}^3$.
Total volume of new cube $A^3 = 729 + 2015 = 2744\text{ cm}^3$.
Side of new cube $A = \sqrt[3]{2744} = 14\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area of new cube $= 6A^2 = 6 \times (14)^2 = 6 \times 196 = 1176\text{ cm}^2$.
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XI: MELTING & RECASTING (CONVERSION OF SOLIDS)
questions.questionText: A woman working in a company was supplied a rectangular solid (cuboid shape) of wax with dimensions $70\text{ cm}, 44\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$ to prepare cylindrical candles, each $14\text{ cm}$ in diameter and $20\text{ cm}$ of height. Find the number of candles.
questions.solution:
Volume of wax block $= 70 \times 44 \times 20 = 61600\text{ cm}^3$.
Candle radius $r = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$, height $h = 20\text{ cm}$.
Volume of one candle $= \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 7^2 \times 20 = 22 \times 7 \times 20 = 3080\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of candles:
$$n = \frac{61600}{3080} = 20$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XII: CONCEPT OF DIGGING & EARTH TAKEN OUT
questions.questionText: A well with inner radius $3\text{ m}$, is dug $6\text{ m}$ deep. The soil taken out of it has been spread evenly all around it to a width of $2\text{ m}$ to form an embankment. The height (in $\text{m}$) of the embankment is:
questions.solution:
Volume of earth taken out $= \pi r^2 h = \pi (3)^2 (6) = 54\pi\text{ m}^3$.
Inner radius of embankment $r = 3\text{ m}$, outer radius $R = 3 + 2 = 5\text{ m}$.
Base area of embankment $= \pi(R^2 - r^2) = \pi(5^2 - 3^2) = 16\pi\text{ m}^2$.
Height of embankment $H$:
$$16\pi H = 54\pi \implies H = \frac{54}{16} = \frac{27}{8} = 3\frac{3}{8}\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XII: CONCEPT OF DIGGING & EARTH TAKEN OUT
questions.questionText: A well with $14\text{ cm}$ radius is dug $23\text{ cm}$ deep. Find the volume of the earth taken out of it.
questions.solution:
Volume of earth taken out $= \pi r^2 h$.
$$V = \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 \times 23 = \frac{22}{7} \times 196 \times 23 = 22 \times 28 \times 23 = 616 \times 23 = 14168\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIII: FILLING A CONTAINER BY ANOTHER SHAPE CONTAINER
questions.questionText: Some medicine in liquid form is prepared in a hemispherical container of diameter $36\text{ cm}$. When the container is full of medicine, the medicine is transferred to small cylindrical bottles of diameter $6\text{ cm}$ and height $6\text{ cm}$. How many bottles are required to empty the container?
questions.solution:
Radius of hemispherical container $R = \frac{36}{2} = 18\text{ cm}$.
Volume of hemispherical container $= \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (18)^3 = 3888\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Radius of cylindrical bottle $r = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ cm}$, height $h = 6\text{ cm}$.
Volume of each cylindrical bottle $= \pi r^2 h = \pi (3)^2 (6) = 54\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of bottles required:
$$n = \frac{3888\pi}{54\pi} = 72$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIII: FILLING A CONTAINER BY ANOTHER SHAPE CONTAINER
questions.questionText: A conical vessel, whose internal radius is $20\text{ cm}$ and height is $27\text{ cm}$, is full of water. If this water is poured into a cylindrical vessel with internal radius $15\text{ cm}$, what will be the height to which the water rises in it?
questions.solution:
Volume of water in conical vessel $= \frac{1}{3}\pi R_c^2 H_c = \frac{1}{3}\pi (20)^2 (27) = 3600\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Let the height of water in the cylindrical vessel be $h$.
Volume of water in cylindrical vessel $= \pi R^2 h = \pi (15)^2 h = 225\pi h$.
Equating volumes:
$$225\pi h = 3600\pi \implies h = \frac{3600}{225} = 16\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIII: FILLING A CONTAINER BY ANOTHER SHAPE CONTAINER
questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius $6\text{ cm}$ contains a liquid. This liquid is to be filled into cylindrical shaped small bottels of diameter $2\text{ cm}$ and height $4\text{ cm}$. How many bottles will be need to empty the bowl?
questions.solution:
Volume of hemispherical bowl $= \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (6)^3 = 144\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Radius of small bottle $r = \frac{2}{2} = 1\text{ cm}$, height $h = 4\text{ cm}$.
Volume of each cylindrical bottle $= \pi r^2 h = \pi (1)^2 (4) = 4\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of bottles required:
$$n = \frac{144\pi}{4\pi} = 36$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIII: FILLING A CONTAINER BY ANOTHER SHAPE CONTAINER
questions.questionText: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius $18\text{ cm}$ is full of liquid. This liquid is to be filled in cylindrical bottles each of radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $6\text{ cm}$. How many bottles are required to empty the bowl?
questions.solution:
Volume of hemispherical bowl $= \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (18)^3 = 3888\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Volume of each cylindrical bottle $= \pi r^2 h = \pi (3)^2 (6) = 54\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of bottles required:
$$n = \frac{3888\pi}{54\pi} = 72$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIII: FILLING A CONTAINER BY ANOTHER SHAPE CONTAINER
questions.questionText: Water is pouring into a cuboidal reservoir at the rate of $50\text{ liters}$ per minute. The volume of the reservoir is $120\text{ m}^3$. How many hours will it take to fill the reservoir?
questions.solution:
Volume of reservoir $= 120\text{ m}^3 = 120 \times 1000 = 120000\text{ liters}$.
Rate of flow $= 50\text{ liters/min} = 50 \times 60 = 3000\text{ liters/hour}$.
Time required to fill the reservoir:
$$t = \frac{120000}{3000} = 40\text{ hours}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIV: CONCEPT OF RISE IN HEIGHT
questions.questionText: A cylinder has some water in it at a height of $16\text{ cm}$. If a sphere of radius $9\text{ cm}$ is put into it, then find the rise in the height of the water if the radius of the cylinder is $12\text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
Volume of sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (9)^3 = 972\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Let the rise in water level in the cylinder be $h$.
Volume of water displaced $= \pi R^2 h = \pi (12)^2 h = 144\pi h$.
Equating volumes:
$$144\pi h = 972\pi \implies h = \frac{972}{144} = \frac{27}{4} = 6.75\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - XIV: CONCEPT OF RISE IN HEIGHT
questions.questionText: Some ice pieces, spherical in shape, of diameter $6\text{ cm}$ are dropped in a cylindrical container containing some juice and are fully submerged. If the diameter of the container is $18\text{ cm}$ and level of juice rises by $40\text{ cm}$, then how many ice pieces are dropped in the container?
questions.solution:
Radius of container $R = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ cm}$, rise in level $h = 40\text{ cm}$.
Volume of raised juice $= \pi R^2 h = \pi (9)^2 (40) = 3240\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Radius of each spherical ice piece $r = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ cm}$.
Volume of each ice piece $= \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3)^3 = 36\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of ice pieces:
$$n = \frac{3240\pi}{36\pi} = 90$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A right circular cone is inscribed in a cube of side $9\text{ cm}$ occupying the maximum space possible. What is the ratio of the volume of the cube to the volume of the cone? $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Let side of cube be $a = 9\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cube $= a^3 = 9^3 = 729\text{ cm}^3$.
For the cone occupying maximum space, base diameter $= a \implies r = \frac{a}{2} = \frac{9}{2}\text{ cm}$, height $h = a = 9\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^2 \times 9 = \frac{11}{42} \times 9^3$.
Mathematically, the ratio of the volume of the cube to that of the cone is:
$$\frac{\text{Volume of cube}}{\text{Volume of cone}} = \frac{a^3}{\frac{11}{42}a^3} = \frac{42}{11}$$
Note: As per the official answer key, option A is marked as correct.
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A solid toy is in the shape which is a combination of a cylinder, cone and a hemispherical bowl. The cylinder contributes to $50\%$ of the total volume of the toy, the cone contributes to $20\%$ of the volume. Find the ratio of the contribution (in terms of volume) of the cone, cylinder and hemisphere.
questions.solution:
Let total volume of the toy be $100\%$.
Volume of cylinder $= 50\%$.
Volume of cone $= 20\%$.
Volume of hemisphere $= 100\% - (50\% + 20\%) = 30\%$.
Ratio of contribution of cone, cylinder and hemisphere:
$$\text{Cone} : \text{Cylinder} : \text{Hemisphere} = 20\% : 50\% : 30\% = 2 : 5 : 3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A largest possible sphere is carved from a cube of side $14\text{ cm}$. What is its volume in $\text{cm}^3$?
questions.solution:
Diameter of the largest sphere carved out of a cube of side $a = 14\text{ cm}$ is $14\text{ cm}$.
Radius of sphere $r = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times 22 \times 49 = \frac{4312}{3} = 1437\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: A sphere passes through the eight corners of a cube of side $14\text{ cm}$. Find the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of the sphere. $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
A sphere passing through the eight corners of a cube circumscribes the cube.
Diameter of sphere $=$ body diagonal of cube $= a\sqrt{3} = 14\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.
Radius of sphere $R = \frac{14\sqrt{3}}{2} = 7\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (7\sqrt{3})^3 = \frac{88}{21} \times 343 \times 3\sqrt{3} = \frac{88}{7} \times 343\sqrt{3} = 88 \times 49\sqrt{3} = 4312\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: Find the volume of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube whose edge is $3\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}$, correct to two places of decimals $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Edge of cube $a = 3\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}$.
Largest cone has base diameter $= a = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm} \implies r = \frac{7}{4}\text{ cm}$, and height $h = a = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 \times \frac{7}{2} = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{49}{16} \times \frac{7}{2} = \frac{11 \times 49}{48} = \frac{539}{48} \approx 11.23\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: For making a toy, a hemisphere is attached at one end of a cylinder and a cone is attached at the other end of the cylinder. The cylinder, the cone and the hemisphere have a common radius of $4.2\text{ cm}$. The height of the cylinder and that of the cone is $7\text{ cm}$. Find the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of the toy. $(\text{Use } \pi = \frac{22}{7})$
questions.solution:
Common radius $r = 4.2\text{ cm}$, height of cylinder $h_1 = 7\text{ cm}$, height of cone $h_2 = 7\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume of toy} = \text{Volume of hemisphere} + \text{Volume of cylinder} + \text{Volume of cone}$$
$$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 + \pi r^2 h_1 + \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h_2 = \pi r^2 \left(\frac{2}{3}r + h_1 + \frac{1}{3}h_2\right)$$
$$\pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 4.2 \times 4.2 = 22 \times 0.6 \times 4.2 = 55.44$$
$$\frac{2}{3}(4.2) + 7 + \frac{7}{3} = 2.8 + 7 + 2.3333 = 12.1333$$
$$V = 55.44 \times 12.1333 = 672.672\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A hemispherical depression of diameter $4\text{ cm}$ is cut out from each face of a cubical block of sides $10\text{ cm}$. Find the surface area of the remaining solid (in $\text{cm}^2$). $[\text{Take } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Cube side $a = 10\text{ cm}$. Radius of each hemispherical depression $r = \frac{4}{2} = 2\text{ cm}$.
On each of the $6$ faces, cutting out a hemispherical depression removes a circular area of $\pi r^2$ and adds a hemispherical curved surface of $2\pi r^2$.
Net change per face $= +\pi r^2$.
For all $6$ faces, total surface area:
$$\text{Total Surface Area} = 6a^2 + 6\pi r^2 = 6(10^2) + 6 \times \frac{22}{7} \times (2)^2 = 600 + \frac{528}{7} = 600 + 75\frac{3}{7} = 675\frac{3}{7}\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The length of the largest possible rod that can be placed in a cubical room is $42\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$. The surface area (in $\text{m}^2$) of the largest possible sphere that fit within the cubical room is: $[\text{Use } \pi = 22/7]$
questions.solution:
Length of the longest rod $=$ body diagonal of cubical room $= a\sqrt{3} = 42\sqrt{3}\text{ m} \implies a = 42\text{ m}$.
Diameter of the largest sphere fitting inside the room $= a = 42\text{ m} \implies r = 21\text{ m}$.
Surface area of the sphere:
$$A = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times (21)^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 63 = 88 \times 63 = 5544\text{ m}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: Find the volume of the largest possible sphere circumscribed by a cube of edge $7\text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
Here 'sphere circumscribed by a cube' refers to the sphere inscribed within the cube.
Diameter of sphere $= 7\text{ cm} \implies r = 3.5\text{ cm} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{343}{8} = \frac{11 \times 49}{3} = \frac{539}{3} \approx 179.67\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The Largest possible sphere is carved out of a cube of side $6\text{ cm}$. What is the volume of the sphere?
questions.solution:
Diameter of sphere $= 6\text{ cm} \implies r = 3\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3^3 = \frac{4 \times 22 \times 9}{7} = \frac{792}{7}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The length of the side of a cube is $5.6\text{ cm}$. What is the volume of the largest sphere that can be taken out of the cube?
questions.solution:
Diameter of the largest sphere $= 5.6\text{ cm} \implies r = 2.8\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (2.8)^3 = \frac{88}{21} \times 21.952 \approx 91.98\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A solid cone of height $42\text{ cm}$ with diameter of its base $42\text{ cm}$ is cut out from a wooden solid sphere of radius $24\text{ cm}$. Find the percentage of wood wasted correct to two places of decimal.
questions.solution:
Radius of sphere $R = 24\text{ cm}$.
Volume of sphere $V_s = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (24)^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (13824) = 18432\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
For cone, base radius $r = \frac{42}{2} = 21\text{ cm}$, height $h = 42\text{ cm}$.
Volume of cone $V_c = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (21)^2 (42) = 6174\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Wasted volume $= 18432\pi - 6174\pi = 12258\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
$$\text{Percentage wasted} = \frac{12258\pi}{18432\pi} \times 100\% = \frac{12258}{18432} \times 100\% \approx 66.50\%$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: What is the volume of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube whose edge is $10\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Edge of cube $a = 10\text{ cm}$.
Diameter of cone base $= a = 10\text{ cm} \implies r = 5\text{ cm}$, height $h = a = 10\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Volume of cone} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (5)^2 (10) = \frac{250\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: From a solid cylindrical wooden block of height $18\text{ cm}$ and radius $7.5\text{ cm}$, a conical cavity of same radius and same height is taken out. What is total surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the remaining solid?
questions.solution:
For the cylinder and conical cavity, $r = 7.5\text{ cm}$ and $h = 18\text{ cm}$.
Slant height of cone $l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{7.5^2 + 18^2} = \sqrt{56.25 + 324} = \sqrt{380.25} = 19.5\text{ cm}$.
Total surface area of remaining solid:
$$\text{TSA} = \text{Base area of cylinder} + \text{Curved surface area of cylinder} + \text{Curved surface area of cone}$$
$$\text{TSA} = \pi r^2 + 2\pi r h + \pi r l = \pi r (r + 2h + l)$$
$$\text{TSA} = \pi (7.5) (7.5 + 2(18) + 19.5) = \pi (7.5)(7.5 + 36 + 19.5) = 7.5 \times 63 \pi = 472.5\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A right circular cylinder of maximum volume is cut out from a solid wooden cube. The material left is what percent of the volume (nearest to an integer) of the original cube?
questions.solution:
Let side of cube be $a$.
Volume of cube $V_{\text{cube}} = a^3$.
For cylinder of maximum volume, base diameter $= a \implies r = \frac{a}{2}$, height $h = a$.
Volume of cylinder $V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2 \times a = \frac{11}{14} a^3$.
Material left $= a^3 - \frac{11}{14} a^3 = \frac{3}{14} a^3$.
$$\text{Percentage left} = \frac{3}{14} \times 100\% = \frac{300}{14}\% \approx 21.43\% \approx 21\%$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A sphere of maximum volume is cut out from a solid hemisphere. What is the ratio of the volume of the sphere to that of the remaining solid?
questions.solution:
Let radius of solid hemisphere be $R$.
Volume of hemisphere $V_{\text{hemi}} = \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3$.
For a sphere of maximum volume carved out of the hemisphere, its diameter equals the height (radius) of the hemisphere:
$$2r = R \implies r = \frac{R}{2}$$
Volume of sphere $V_{\text{sph}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi \left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{6}\pi R^3$.
Volume of remaining solid $= V_{\text{hemi}} - V_{\text{sph}} = \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3 - \frac{1}{6}\pi R^3 = \frac{1}{2}\pi R^3$.
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{V_{\text{sph}}}{V_{\text{rem}}} = \frac{\frac{1}{6}\pi R^3}{\frac{1}{2}\pi R^3} = \frac{1/6}{1/2} = \frac{1}{3} = 1 : 3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: A right triangle with sides $3\text{ cm}, 4\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$ is rotated about the sides of $3\text{ cm}$ to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
questions.solution:
When rotated about the side of $3\text{ cm}$, that side forms the height of the cone ($h = 3\text{ cm}$), and the side of $4\text{ cm}$ forms the base radius ($r = 4\text{ cm}$).
$$\text{Volume of cone} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (4)^2 (3) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: Two rectangular sheets of paper, each $60\text{ cm} \times 36\text{ cm}$, are made into two right circular cylinders, one by rolling the paper along its length and the other along the breadth. The ratio of the volumes of the two cylinders, thus formed, is:
questions.solution:
Case 1: Rolled along length ($60\text{ cm}$):
Circumference $2\pi r_1 = 60 \implies r_1 = \frac{60}{2\pi}$, height $h_1 = 36\text{ cm}$.
$$V_1 = \pi r_1^2 h_1 = \pi \left(\frac{60}{2\pi}\right)^2 (36) = \frac{3600 \times 36}{4\pi}$$
Case 2: Rolled along breadth ($36\text{ cm}$):
Circumference $2\pi r_2 = 36 \implies r_2 = \frac{36}{2\pi}$, height $h_2 = 60\text{ cm}$.
$$V_2 = \pi r_2^2 h_2 = \pi \left(\frac{36}{2\pi}\right)^2 (60) = \frac{1296 \times 60}{4\pi}$$
Ratio of volumes:
$$\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{3600 \times 36}{1296 \times 60} = \frac{60 \times 36}{1296} = \frac{2160}{1296} = \frac{5}{3} = 5 : 3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: A rectangular piece of paper is $50\text{ cm}$ long and $22\text{ cm}$ wide. If a cylinder is formed by rolling the paper along its breadth, then the volume of the cylinder is:
questions.solution:
Rolling along breadth implies base circumference $2\pi r = 22\text{ cm}$ and cylinder height $h = 50\text{ cm}$.
$$2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 22 \implies r = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Volume} = \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2 \times 50 = \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{49}{4} \times 50 = \frac{154 \times 50}{4} = 1925\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle whose side is $10\text{ cm}$. If height of this prism is $10\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, then what is the total surface area of prism?
questions.solution:
Side of equilateral triangle base $a = 10\text{ cm}$, height $h = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.
Base area $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (10)^2 = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.
Base perimeter $= 3 \times 10 = 30\text{ cm}$.
Lateral surface area $= \text{perimeter} \times h = 30 \times 10\sqrt{3} = 300\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{TSA} = \text{LSA} + 2 \times \text{Base area} = 300\sqrt{3} + 2(25\sqrt{3}) = 350\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: Let $ABCDEF$ is prism whose base is a right triangle whose perpendicular sides are $9\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$, if cost of painting the prism is $₹151.20$ at the rate of $20\text{ paise/cm}^2$ then find the height of the prism?
questions.solution:
Total cost of painting $= ₹151.20 = 15120\text{ paise}$.
$$\text{Total Surface Area (TSA)} = \frac{15120}{20} = 756\text{ cm}^2$$
For the right triangle base with legs $9\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Hypotenuse} = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Base area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 12 = 54\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Base perimeter} = 9 + 12 + 15 = 36\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{TSA} = (\text{Base perimeter} \times h) + 2 \times \text{Base area}$$
$$756 = 36h + 2(54) = 36h + 108$$
$$36h = 756 - 108 = 648 \implies h = \frac{648}{36} = 18\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The base of a prism is a right angle triangle whose sides are $9\text{ cm}, 12\text{ cm}$ and $15\text{ cm}$. Volume of this prism is $648\text{ cm}^3$. What will be the height of prism?
questions.solution:
Base area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 12 = 54\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{Volume} = \text{Base area} \times h$$
$$648 = 54 \times h \implies h = \frac{648}{54} = 12\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle whose each side is $4\text{ cm}$. If the lateral surface area is $120\text{ cm}^2$, find the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of the prism.
questions.solution:
Base perimeter $= 3 \times 4 = 12\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Lateral surface area} = \text{perimeter} \times h = 12 \times h = 120 \implies h = 10\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Base area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (4)^2 = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Volume} = \text{Base area} \times h = 4\sqrt{3} \times 10 = 40\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The base of a solid prism of height $10\text{ cm}$ is a square and its volume is $160\text{ cm}^3$, What is its total surface area of the prism (in $\text{cm}^2$ ) ?
questions.solution:
Let side of square base be $a$.
$$\text{Volume} = a^2 \times h = a^2 \times 10 = 160 \implies a^2 = 16 \implies a = 4\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Total Surface Area} = 2a^2 + 4ah = 2(16) + 4(4)(10) = 32 + 160 = 192\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The base of a right prism is a triangle with sides $16\text{ cm}, 30\text{ cm}$ and $34\text{ cm}$. Its height is $32\text{ cm}$. The lateral surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) and the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) are, respectively:
questions.solution:
Since $16^2 + 30^2 = 256 + 900 = 1156 = 34^2$, the base is a right triangle.
$$\text{Base area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 30 = 240\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Base perimeter} = 16 + 30 + 34 = 80\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Lateral surface area} = \text{perimeter} \times h = 80 \times 32 = 2560\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Volume} = \text{Base area} \times h = 240 \times 32 = 7680\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: The base of right prism is a trapezium whose parallel sides are $11\text{cm}$ and $15\text{cm}$ and the distance between them is $9\text{ cm}$. If the volume of the prism is $1731.6\text{ cm}^3$, then the height (in $\text{cm}$) of the prism will be :
questions.solution:
Base area of trapezium $= \frac{1}{2} (a + b) \times d = \frac{1}{2}(11 + 15) \times 9 = 13 \times 9 = 117\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{Volume} = \text{Base area} \times h$$
$$1731.6 = 117 \times h \implies h = \frac{1731.6}{117} = 14.8\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The base of a right prism is a regular hexagon of side $5\text{ cm}$. If its height is $12\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, then its volume ( in $\text{cm}^3$) is:
questions.solution:
Base area of regular hexagon $= 6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = 6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (5^2) = \frac{75\sqrt{3}}{2}\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{Volume} = \text{Base area} \times h = \frac{75\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12\sqrt{3} = 75 \times 3 \times 6 = 1350\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The base of a right prism is a triangle with sides $20\text{ cm}, 21\text{ cm}$ and $29\text{ cm}$. If its volume is $7560\text{ cm}^3$, then its lateral surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) is :
questions.solution:
Since $20^2 + 21^2 = 400 + 441 = 841 = 29^2$, the base is a right triangle.
$$\text{Base area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 21 = 210\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Volume} = \text{Base area} \times h \implies 7560 = 210 \times h \implies h = \frac{7560}{210} = 36\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Base perimeter} = 20 + 21 + 29 = 70\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Lateral surface area} = \text{perimeter} \times h = 70 \times 36 = 2520\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The base of a right pyramid is an equilateral triangle with area $16\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$. If the area of one of its lateral faces is $30\text{ cm}^2$, then its height (in $\text{cm}$) is:
questions.solution:
Base area of equilateral triangle $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = 16\sqrt{3} \implies a^2 = 64 \implies a = 8\text{ cm}$.
Area of one lateral face $= \frac{1}{2} \times a \times l = 30$, where $l$ is slant height.
$$\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times l = 30 \implies 4l = 30 \implies l = \frac{15}{2}\text{ cm}$$
Inradius of equilateral base $r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{8}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Height } h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{225}{4} - \frac{16}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{675 - 64}{12}} = \sqrt{\frac{611}{12}}\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The base of right pyramid is an equilateral triangle, each side of which is $20\text{ cm}$. Each slant edge is $30\text{ cm}$. The vertical height (in $\text{cm}$) of the pyramid is:
questions.solution:
Side of equilateral base $a = 20\text{ cm}$, slant edge $e = 30\text{ cm}$.
Circumradius of the base $R = \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{20}{\sqrt{3}}\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Vertical height } h = \sqrt{e^2 - R^2} = \sqrt{30^2 - \left(\frac{20}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2} = \sqrt{900 - \frac{400}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{2300}{3}} = 10\sqrt{\frac{23}{3}}\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is D.

questions.questionText: What is the total surface area of a pyramid whose base is a square with side $8\text{ cm}$ and height of the pyramid is $3\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Side of square base $a = 8\text{ cm}$, height $h = 3\text{ cm}$.
Distance from center to edge of base $= \frac{a}{2} = 4\text{ cm}$.
Slant height $l = \sqrt{h^2 + \left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{LSA} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Perimeter} \times l = \frac{1}{2} \times (4 \times 8) \times 5 = 80\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Base area} = a^2 = 8^2 = 64\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{TSA} = \text{LSA} + \text{Base area} = 80 + 64 = 144\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText: The base of a pyramid is a regular polygon, whose total surface area is $340\text{ cm}^2$, and area of base is $100\text{ cm}^2$, if area of each lateral surface is $30\text{ cm}^2$, then find no. of lateral surfaces of pyramid?
questions.solution:
Total lateral surface area $= \text{TSA} - \text{Base area} = 340 - 100 = 240\text{ cm}^2$.
Since area of each lateral surface is $30\text{ cm}^2$:
$$\text{Number of lateral surfaces} = \frac{240}{30} = 8$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The base of a pyramid is an equilateral triangle whose each side is $8\text{ cm}$. Its slant edge is $24\text{ cm}$. What is the total surface area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the pyramid?
questions.solution:
Side of equilateral triangle $a = 8\text{ cm}$, slant edge $e = 24\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Base area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (8^2) = 16\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$
Each lateral face is an isosceles triangle with base $8\text{ cm}$ and sides $24\text{ cm}$.
Slant height $l = \sqrt{e^2 - \left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{24^2 - 4^2} = \sqrt{576 - 16} = \sqrt{560} = 4\sqrt{35}\text{ cm}$.
Area of $3$ lateral faces $= 3 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 4\sqrt{35}\right) = 48\sqrt{35}\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{TSA} = 16\sqrt{3} + 48\sqrt{35} = (16\sqrt{3} + 48\sqrt{35})\text{ cm}^2$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The total surface area of a right pyramid, with base as a square of side $8\text{ cm}$, is $208\text{ cm}^2$. What is the slant height (in $\text{cm}$) of the pyramid?
questions.solution:
Base area of square $= 8^2 = 64\text{ cm}^2$.
$$\text{Lateral surface area} = \text{TSA} - \text{Base area} = 208 - 64 = 144\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{LSA} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Perimeter} \times l$$
$$144 = \frac{1}{2} \times (4 \times 8) \times l = 16l \implies l = \frac{144}{16} = 9\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: The base of a right pyramid is a square of side $8\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ and each of its slant edge is of length $10\text{ cm}$. What is the volume (in $\text{cm}^3$) of the pyramid?
questions.solution:
Base is square of side $a = 8\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Base area} = a^2 = (8\sqrt{2})^2 = 128\text{ cm}^2$$
Diagonal of square base $= a\sqrt{2} = 8\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2} = 16\text{ cm}$.
Distance from corner to center of base $= \frac{16}{2} = 8\text{ cm}$.
Slant edge $e = 10\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Height } h = \sqrt{e^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{Base area} \times h = \frac{1}{3} \times 128 \times 6 = 256\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: The volume of a right pyramid is $45\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^3$ and its base is an equilateral triangle with side $6\text{ cm}$. What is the height (in $\text{cm}$) of the pyramid ?
questions.solution:
Base is equilateral triangle with side $a = 6\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Base area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (6^2) = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{Base area} \times h = \frac{1}{3} \times 9\sqrt{3} \times h = 3\sqrt{3}h$$
Equating volumes:
$$3\sqrt{3}h = 45\sqrt{3} \implies h = 15\text{ cm}$$
Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.questionText: A prism and a pyramid have the same base and the same height. Find the ratio of the volumes of the prism and the pyramid.
questions.solution:
Let base area be $B$ and height be $h$.
Volume of prism $V_{\text{prism}} = B \times h$.
Volume of pyramid $V_{\text{pyramid}} = \frac{1}{3} B \times h$.
$$\frac{V_{\text{prism}}}{V_{\text{pyramid}}} = \frac{B \times h}{\frac{1}{3} B \times h} = \frac{3}{1} = 3 : 1$$
Hence, the correct option is B.

questions.questionText: A right square pyramid having lateral surface area is $624\text{ cm}^2$. If the length of the diagonal of the square is $24\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$, then the volume of the pyramid is:
questions.solution:
Diagonal of square base $= a\sqrt{2} = 24\sqrt{2}\text{ cm} \implies a = 24\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Base area} = a^2 = 24^2 = 576\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Base perimeter} = 4 \times 24 = 96\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Lateral surface area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Perimeter} \times l = 624$$
$$\frac{1}{2} \times 96 \times l = 624 \implies 48l = 624 \implies l = 13\text{ cm}$$
Distance from center to edge of base $= \frac{a}{2} = 12\text{ cm}$.
$$\text{Height } h = \sqrt{l^2 - \left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{Base area} \times h = \frac{1}{3} \times 576 \times 5 = 192 \times 5 = 960\text{ cm}^3$$
Hence, the correct option is D.
